reason.en: Burden shifts only after the plaintiff proves each defendant was negligent.
reason.zh: 仅在原告证明各被告均有过失后，举证责任才会转移。

reason.en: Parents baked separately at home and were not pursuing a common plan or design.
reason.zh: 家长各自在家烘焙，并非依共同计划或设计行事。

highlights.text: claiming that the parents are jointly and severally liable for her harm

reason.en: Frames the legal theory the student must establish against all three parents.
reason.zh: 界定学生须对三名家长主张的法律责任类型。

highlights.text: someone who made the cookies did not follow appropriate food-safety measures

reason.en: Limits the negligence finding to one unknown parent, not each defendant.
reason.zh: 过失认定仅指向一名未知家长，而非各被告均有过失。

highlights.text: not which specific parent made the contaminated cookies

reason.en: Creates indivisible harm but does not eliminate the need to prove each parent's negligence.
reason.zh: 虽形成不可分损害，但仍须证明各家长均有过失。

highlights.text: Three parents separately made chocolate chip cookies at their own homes, following their own recipes

reason.en: Undermines any acting-in-concert basis for joint liability.
reason.zh: 排除以共同行为作为连带责任基础的可能。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A politician and a businessman were passengers sitting in adjoining seats on an airline's flight. There were many empty seats on the aircraft.
During the flight, a flight attendant served the businessman eight drinks. As the businessman became more and more obviously intoxicated and attempted to engage the politician in a conversation, the politician chose to ignore the businessman. This angered the businessman, who suddenly struck the politician in the face, giving her a black eye.
If the politician asserts a claim for damages against the airline based on battery, will she prevail?

choices.A: No, because the businessman was not acting as an agent or employee of the airline.
choices.B: No, unless she can establish some permanent injury from the contact.
choices.C: Yes, because she suffered an intentionally inflicted harmful or offensive contact.
choices.D: Yes, if the flight attendant acted recklessly in continuing to serve liquor to the businessman.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Vicarious liability
(liability for tortious acts of another)
Respondeat superior Employee's conduct occurred within scope of employment—ie, under employer's control or while performing assigned work
Nondelegable duty Independent contractor's work involved abnormally or inherently dangerous activity, condition on land open to general public, or activity regulated by law
Parent Child committed tort while acting as parent's agent
Business partner Business partner's conduct occurred within scope of business
Automobile owner Family member drove car with permission (family-car doctrine) or any person drove car with permission under owner-liability statute
Dram shop & social host Alcohol sold (dram shop) or served at noncommercial setting (social liability) to visibly intoxicated person or minor

*Only applies when question provides dram-shop statute.

Vicarious liability is a type of strict liability in which a principal is liable for the tortious act (e.g., battery) of his/her agent if the act was committed within the scope of an agency relationship. An agency relationship exists when the parties mutually agree that the agent will act on the principal's behalf and subject to the principal's control (e.g., employer-employee).

Here, the businessman intentionally struck the politician in the face (battery) on the airline's flight. But since the businessman was not an employee of the airline or otherwise acting on its behalf (no agency relationship), the airline is not vicariously liable for the businessman's battery. Therefore, the politician will not prevail in her battery claim against the airline.

(Choice B) Battery merely requires proof of harmful or offensive contact—not permanent injury. Therefore, the politician's ability to show permanent injury will not affect the success of her claim against the airline. Instead, her claim will fail because the airline is not vicariously liable for the businessman's conduct.

(Choice C) The fact that the politician suffered an intentionally inflicted harmful or offensive contact when the businessman struck her face would support a battery claim against the businessman. But since the businessman was not the airline's agent, this fact will not allow the politician to prevail against the airline.

(Choice D) The airline could be vicariously liable for the flight attendant's (i.e., an employee's) negligence or recklessness in continuing to serve liquor to the businessman. But since the politician's battery claim against the airline is based on the businessman's conduct—not the flight attendant's negligence—the politician's claim will fail.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is vicariously liable for a tort committed by his/her agent if the tort was committed within the scope of an agency relationship. An agency relationship exists when both parties agree that the agent will act on the principal's behalf and subject to the principal's control (e.g., employer-employee).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency § 7.03 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (principal's liability for acts of its agents).
questions.zh-question:
一名政治家和一名商人是某航空公司航班上邻座的乘客。飞机上有很多空座位。

在飞行途中，一名空中乘务员为该商人上了八杯酒。当该商人变得越来越明显醉酒并试图与政治家交谈时，政治家选择不理睬他。这激怒了该商人，他突然打了政治家的脸，导致她眼部瘀青。

如果该政治家基于伤害罪向航空公司主张损害赔偿，她会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该商人并非作为航空公司的代理人或雇员行事。
zh-choices.B: 不会，除非她能证明此次接触造成了某种永久性伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为她遭受了故意造成的有害或冒犯性接触。
zh-choices.D: 会，如果空中乘务员在持续为该商人提供含酒精饮料方面的行为构成鲁莽。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Vicarious Liability
核心法律原则

本题考察的核心是替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)，特别是雇主对雇员行为的责任原则 (Respondeat Superior)。

关键规则：只有当侵权人是被告的代理人 (Agent) 或 雇员 (Employee)，且该行为发生在代理/雇佣范围 (Scope of Employment) 内时，被告才需承担替代责任。

案情回顾：一名醉酒乘客（商人）殴打了另一名乘客（政治家）。政治家起诉航空公司，诉由是殴打 (Battery)。

深度解析
正确答案 A

理由： 殴打 (Battery) 是一种故意侵权行为 (Intentional Tort)。这起殴打是由商人实施的。

要让航空公司对商人的行为负责，必须证明商人是航空公司的代理人或雇员。显然，商人只是付费乘客，与航空公司之间不存在代理关系。因此，航空公司无需对乘客的个人犯罪/侵权行为承担替代责任。

陷阱选项 D

为什么这是最大的干扰项？

很多考生会选 D，因为乘务员给醉酒乘客提供酒精确实可能构成过失 (Negligence)。如果题目问的是“航空公司是否因过失承担责任”，D 可能是对的。

但是：题目明确指出政治家的诉由是基于殴打 (Based on Battery)。航空公司并没有实施殴打，实施殴打的人也不是航空公司的员工。因此，基于殴打的索赔无法成立。

选项 B

错误点： 殴打 (Battery) 的构成要件仅要求“有害或冒犯性的接触” (Harmful or offensive contact)，并不要求造成永久性伤害 (Permanent injury)。即使没有永久伤害，殴打罪名依然成立，但这不能解决航空公司是否承担责任的问题。

🎓 MBE 提分技巧：

仔细阅读题干中的诉由 (Cause of Action)！

本题中，如果原告起诉的是“过失” (Negligence)，结果可能完全不同（因为乘务员的行为可能违反了注意义务）。但既然起诉的是“殴打” (Battery)，你必须专注于谁实施了殴打，以及被告是否对该人有替代责任。
MBE Torts Review | Vicarious Liability

A.text: agent or employee of the airline

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man's dog ran into the street in front of his home and began chasing cars. The man had seen the dog behave similarly on several prior occasions. A ride-share driver, who was driving a car on the street, swerved to avoid hitting the dog, struck a telephone pole, and was injured.
There is no statute or ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed on a public street.
If the driver asserts a claim against the man, will the driver prevail?

choices.A: No, because a dog is a domestic animal.
choices.B: No, because no statute or ordinance made it unlawful for the owner to allow a dog to be unleashed on a public street.
choices.C: Yes, because the man is strictly liable for injuries caused by his dog.
choices.D: Yes, because the man knew his dog had a propensity to chase cars and did not restrain it.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Elements of negligence
  • Duty – defendant owed duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – defendant breached duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – defendant's breach actually & proximately caused plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

Negligence is the typical tort claim for unintentional harms (eg, car-accident injuries). To prevail on a negligence claim, the plaintiff must prove all of the following elements by a preponderance of the evidence:

  • Duty – the defendant owed a duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created a foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – the defendant breached that duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – the defendant's breach actually and proximately caused the plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – the plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

A defendant fails to use reasonable care when he/she does not take reasonable steps to reduce the risk posed by his/her conduct.

Here, the man had a duty to use reasonable care since he knew that his dog had a propensity to chase cars. But he breached that duty when he failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the dog from running into the street (eg, by restraining it). And since this caused the driver to crash and sustain injuries, the driver will likely prevail.

(Choices A & C) The owner of a domestic animal is not strictly liable for injuries caused by that animal unless the owner knew, or should have known, that the animal had propensities that are more dangerous than normal for the species. So here, the dog's mere propensity to chase cars would not subject the man to strict liability. But the man is still subject to negligence liability for injuries caused by his dog.

(Choice B) Had the man violated a statute or ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed on public streets, his negligent conduct could be presumed under the doctrine of negligence per se. But the man's negligent conduct can still be proved since he knew of his dog's propensity to chase cars and did not restrain it.

📌 Educational Objective

Persons owe a duty of reasonable care when their conduct poses a foreseeable risk of harm to others. Therefore, persons who fail to take reasonable steps to mitigate that risk and cause another physical harm are liable for negligence.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 281 cmt. e (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that conduct is negligent when it tends to subject another to an unreasonable risk of harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子的狗在他家门前的街道上跑，并开始追逐汽车。该男子曾多次看到这只狗有类似的行为。一名在街上开车的网约车司机，为了躲避这只狗而急转弯，撞上了一根电线杆并受伤。

没有法律或法令要求在公共街道上必须用狗绳拴住狗。

如果司机对该男子提起诉讼，司机会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为狗是家养动物。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为没有法律或法令规定主人在公共街道上不给狗拴绳是违法的。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子对他的狗造成的伤害负有严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该男子知道他的狗有追逐汽车的习性，但没有对其进行约束。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence & Animals

✅ 正确答案：D

会胜诉，因为该男子知道他的狗有追逐汽车的习性，但没有对其进行约束。

⚖️ 核心法律逻辑解析
1

过失责任 (Negligence)

本题的核心在于普通法下的过失责任。要证明过失，原告需证明四个要素：

  • Duty (义务)：被告有采取合理注意的义务。
  • Breach (违约)：被告未能采取合理措施。
  • Causation (因果关系)：被告的行为导致了损害。
  • Damages (损害)：原告遭受了实际伤害。
2

知情即产生义务 (Knowledge Creates Duty)

这是本题的关键考点（Key Issue）：

虽然没有法律规定必须拴狗，但因为主人知道（Actual Knowledge）这只狗以前有追逐汽车的习性，这就创造了一个可预见的风险（Foreseeable Risk）。

一旦风险可预见，主人就负有合理注意义务（Duty of Reasonable Care）去防止这种风险发生（例如拴住狗）。未能做到这一点，即构成过失。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误：
虽然狗是家养动物（Domestic Animal），但这并不意味着主人有“免死金牌”。家养动物的主人如果未能尽到合理注意义务，仍然要承担过失责任。
选项 B 错误 (陷阱)：
这是关于 Negligence Per Se（本身过失）的考点。虽然没有违反法规（Statute），但这只意味着原告不能直接利用法规来推定过失。原告仍然可以通过证明被告违反了普通法上的合理注意义务（Common Law Duty of Care）来胜诉。
选项 C 错误 (易混淆)：
这涉及 Strict Liability（严格责任）。对于家养动物，只有当主人知道其有异常危险的习性（Abnormally Dangerous Propensities，如咬人）时，才适用严格责任。

虽然追车很危险，但在MBE的逻辑中，这通常被归类为需要主人行使注意义务的过失范畴，而不是自动触发严格责任。即使不适用严格责任，过失责任（选项D）也是更稳妥、更直接的胜诉理由。
在处理动物致害题目时，请按以下步骤思考：
  1. 是野生动物还是家养动物？ 野生动物通常适用严格责任。
  2. 如果是家养动物，主人是否知情？
    如果主人知道动物有危险习性（One-bite rule）→ 可能适用严格责任。
    如果主人知道动物有某种行为会造成风险（如追车）→ 适用过失责任 (Negligence)。
  3. 不要被“无法律规定”迷惑： 即使没有违反成文法，普通法下的注意义务依然存在。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A homeowner resides downhill from a metal fabrication facility. She has sued both the owner of the facility and the supplier of a solvent used at the facility. She contends that contaminants, consisting mostly of the solvent, were released into the ground at the facility and have migrated and continue to migrate to her property, contaminating the soil, the groundwater, and her well. She alleges various acts of negligence on the part of the facility owner in causing the release of the contaminants into the ground. She also alleges that employees of the solvent supplier were negligent in frequently spilling some of the solvent onto the ground while filling a rooftop tank at the facility.
The solvent supplier has moved for summary judgment, arguing that if there was any contamination, the facility owner and the supplier independently contributed indeterminate amounts to the contamination and that therefore the homeowner cannot show how much damage each has inflicted on her.
There is no evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert.
Should the court grant the summary judgment motion?

choices.A: No, because concurrent tortfeasors are jointly and severally liable for an indivisible injury.
choices.B: No, because the solvent supplier is vicariously liable for damage inflicted by the facility owner.
choices.C: Yes, because there is no basis for allocating damages against the solvent supplier.
choices.D: Yes, because there is no evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert.

questions.explanation:
Liability of multiple negligent actors
Indivisible injuriesSeparable injuries
Acting independentlyJoint & several liability*Several liability only
Acting in concertJoint & several liability
*Default rule on MBE.

A movant is entitled to summary judgment when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law—eg, when the nonmovant fails to prove his/her claim. A claim for negligence requires proof that a tortfeasor's conduct actually and proximately caused the alleged harm. If the harm was caused by multiple tortfeasors, then those tortfeasors can be held:

  • severally liable – when each tortfeasor is liable for a proportionate amount of damages because his/her independent actions caused separable injuries or
  • jointly and severally liable – when any tortfeasor can be held liable for the total amount of damages because his/her independent or concerted actions concurrently caused an indivisible injury.

Here, the solvent supplier's motion for summary judgment alleges that both parties contributed indeterminate amounts to the contamination. This allegation shows that the homeowner suffered an indivisible injury, so either the solvent supplier or the facility owner can be held jointly and severally liable for all of her harm—even though they did not act in concert. As a result, the solvent supplier is not entitled to judgment as a matter of law, and the court should deny its summary judgment motion (Choice C).

*When a plaintiff recovers the full amount of damages from any one of the tortfeasors, that tortfeasor can then sue the others for indemnity or contribution.

(Choice B) Under vicarious liability, a principal is strictly liable for its agent's tortious acts committed within the scope of an agency relationship (eg, employer-employee). Here, the solvent supplier is vicariously liable for the damage caused by its employees—but not for the damage caused by the facility owner.

(Choice D) Joint and several liability applies if the concerted or independent acts of multiple tortfeasors concurrently caused an indivisible injury. Therefore, evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert is not required.

📌 Educational Objective

When multiple tortfeasors caused the plaintiff harm, each will be liable for a proportionate amount of damages if his/her independent actions caused separable injuries (ie, several liability) OR for the total amount if their independent or concerted actions concurrently caused an indivisible injury (ie, joint and several liability).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § A18 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (joint & several liability).
questions.zh-question:
一位房主居住在一家金属制造厂的下游。她同时起诉了该工厂的厂主和该工厂所用溶剂的供应商。她声称，主要由溶剂构成的污染物在该工厂被排放到地下，并且已经迁移并继续迁移到她的房产，污染了土壤、地下水和她的水井。她指控工厂厂主在导致污染物排放到地下的过程中有多种过失行为。她还指控溶剂供应商的雇员在给工厂的屋顶储罐注水时，因经常将部分溶剂洒到地上而存在过失。

溶剂供应商已提出简易判决动议，辩称如果存在任何污染，工厂厂主和供应商是独立地造成了不确定数量的污染，因此房主无法证明各方对她造成了多少损害。

没有证据表明工厂厂主和溶剂供应商是共同行动的。

法院是否应批准该简易判决动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为并发侵权行为人对不可分割的损害承担连带责任。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为溶剂供应商对工厂厂主造成的损害负有替代责任。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为没有向溶剂供应商分配损害赔偿的依据。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为没有证据表明工厂厂主和溶剂供应商是共同行动的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Joint and Several Liability
⚖️ 核心法则：连带责任 (Joint and Several Liability)

在MBE考试中，关于多名侵权行为人（Multiple Tortfeasors）的责任分配，遵循以下默认规则：

行为性质 损害类型 责任形式
共同行为
(Acting in Concert)		 任何损害 连带责任
(Joint & Several)
独立行为
(Acting Independently)		 不可分割
(Indivisible Injury)		 连带责任
(Joint & Several)
独立行为
(Acting Independently)		 可分割
(Separable Injury)		 按份责任
(Several Liability)

🔍 案情关键点分析

本题中，被告（溶剂供应商）试图通过简易判决 (Summary Judgment) 结案，理由是：

  1. 工厂主和供应商是独立行动的（非共同行为）。
  2. 他们各自造成的污染量是不确定的 (Indeterminate)。

法律推理：

被告的辩护恰恰证明了原告遭受的是一种不可分割的损害 (Indivisible Injury)。地下水污染通常混合在一起，无法区分哪一滴毒药来自哪一个被告。

根据侵权法原则，当两个或多个被告的独立过失行为结合在一起，造成了单一的、不可分割的损害时，他们被视为并发侵权行为人 (Concurrent Tortfeasors)，并对全部损害承担连带责任。

✅ 正确答案解析

选项 A 不应批准，因为并发侵权行为人对不可分割的损害承担连带责任。

这是对法律规则的直接应用。既然损害无法分割（Indeterminate amounts），原告无需证明每个被告具体造成了多少比例的损害。原告可以向任何一个被告索赔全部损失。

注：赔偿全额后的被告可以向其他被告寻求分担 (Contribution)。

❌ 错误选项排除

选项 B 替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)

替代责任通常适用于雇主对雇员的行为负责。供应商不对工厂主的行为负责。这里的关键不是替代责任，而是基于不可分割损害的连带责任。

选项 C 没有分配依据

这正是连带责任要解决的问题。如果无法分配，风险由过失的被告承担，而不是由无辜的原告承担。被告不能因为无法计算具体份额就逃避责任。

选项 D 没有共同行动 (Concert of Action)

这是一个陷阱。虽然共同行动会导致连带责任，但它不是连带责任的唯一来源。如上表所示，独立行为造成不可分割损害同样适用连带责任。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到“有毒物质泄漏”、“火灾汇合”或“多车连环相撞”导致无法区分具体伤害来源的题目时：
1. 判定损害是否不可分割 (Indivisible)。
2. 如果是，哪怕被告互不认识、独立行动，默认规则也是连带责任 (Joint and Several Liability)。
3. 此时，被告关于“无法确定我造成了多少伤害”的辩解是无效的，甚至是对原告有利的证据。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A farmer owns a large farm on which he allows his friends to hunt during quail-hunting season. He does not provide his friends with any instructions about gun safety. The neighbor who owns property adjacent to the farm knows of the friends' use of the property during the hunting season.
One day during the hunting season, without the farmer's knowledge or permission, the neighbor took a shortcut across the farm to visit an acquaintance. The neighbor was wounded by a shot fired by one of the farmer's friends, who was shooting at quail and carelessly failed to see the neighbor.
Traditional rules of landowners' and occupiers' liability apply.
In an action by the neighbor against the farmer to recover for the injuries, will the neighbor be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the farmer is not responsible for his friends' conduct.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor was trespassing.
choices.C: Yes, because the careless friend was permitted to hunt without safety training.
choices.D: Yes, because the use of firearms is an abnormally dangerous activity.

questions.explanation:
Land possessor's duty to land entrants
(traditional approach)*
Status Characteristics Duty
Trespasser
  • Intentionally enters land without permission
  • Known or frequent trespassers — warn of known artificial dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
  • Unknown or unanticipated trespassers — no duty
Licensee
  • Enters land with permission (eg, social guest)
  • Warn of known latent dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
Invitee
  • Enters land open to public (eg, churchgoer)
  • Enters land for business purpose (eg, store customer)
  • Inspect for unknown dangers
  • Make premises safe or provide adequate warnings
  • Prevent harm from active operations

*In jurisdictions that follow the modern approach, land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants, except flagrant trespassers.

Under the traditional approach, persons who occupy and control land (ie, land possessors) owe foreseeable land entrants a duty to exercise reasonable care. But a land possessor owes no duty to trespassers—those who intentionally enter another's land without permission—unless the land possessor knows of, or can reasonably anticipate, their presence. The land possessor is then liable for negligence if he/she breaches this duty and causes the trespasser physical harm.

Here, the neighbor was a trespasser since the neighbor intentionally entered the farmer's land without permission. And the farmer did not know that the neighbor was on the farmer's land. Nor is there any indication that the farmer had reason to anticipate the neighbor's presence (eg, from frequently witnessing the neighbor cut across the farm). As a result, the farmer did not owe his neighbor a duty of care, and the neighbor is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice A) Although the farmer is not responsible (ie, vicariously liable) for his friends' conduct, the farmer could have been liable for his own negligent conduct if he had owed his neighbor a duty (not seen here).

(Choice C) Had the neighbor been a foreseeable land entrant, the farmer would have owed the neighbor a duty to use reasonable care in active operations on the farm—eg, by ensuring that his friends had gun-safety training. But since the neighbor was an unknown and unanticipated trespasser, the farmer owed the neighbor no duty.

(Choice D) Using firearms in rural areas during hunting season is not an abnormally dangerous activity that subjects a defendant to strict liability—ie, liability imposed regardless of fault—since this is a common activity whose risks can be mitigated by reasonable care.

📌 Educational Objective

A land possessor only owes a duty of reasonable care to foreseeable land entrants—not unforeseeable ones (eg, unknown and unanticipated trespassers).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 333 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (no duty to unknown trespassers).
questions.zh-question:
一个农民拥有一个大农场，在鹌鹑狩猎季节，他允许朋友们在农场上打猎。他没有向朋友们提供任何关于枪支安全的指导。拥有与该农场相邻地产的邻居知道，在狩猎季节，农民的朋友们会使用这片土地。

狩猎季节的一天，邻居在未经农民知情或许可的情况下，抄近道穿过农场去拜访一位熟人。邻居被农民的一位朋友开枪射伤，当时这位朋友正在射击鹌鹑，并因疏忽而未能看到邻居。

本案适用土地所有者和占有者的传统责任规则。

在邻居向农民提起的旨在就其伤害获得赔偿的诉讼中，邻居是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为农民不对其朋友的行为承担责任。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为邻居是非法侵入者。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为那个疏忽的朋友在未受过安全培训的情况下被允许打猎。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为使用枪支是一种异常危险的活动。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 侵权法考点解析

Landowner Liability (土地所有者责任)
✅ 正确答案：B 不会，因为邻居是非法侵入者 (Trespasser)。

本题的核心考点是土地占有者对不同类型进入者的注意义务 (Duty of Care)。题目明确指出适用“传统规则 (Traditional Rules)”。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

在传统规则下，原告在土地上的身份 (Status) 决定了被告对其负有的义务层级：

  • 未被发现的非法侵入者 (Undiscovered Trespasser)：
    无注意义务 (No Duty)。
    土地所有者无需警告危险，也无需在活动中采取合理注意。
  • 已被发现/预见的非法侵入者 (Discovered/Anticipated Trespasser)：
    有义务警告已知的人为死亡陷阱 (Man-made death traps)，并在“积极活动 (Active Operations)”中采取合理注意。
  • 被许可人 (Licensee) & 受邀人 (Invitee)：
    负有更高程度的注意义务。
🔍 案情具体分析

1. 确定原告身份：

邻居是在“未经农民知情或许可 (without the farmer's knowledge or permission)”的情况下进入农场的。且没有任何事实表明邻居经常抄近道，因此农民无法预见其存在。

👉 结论：邻居属于未被发现的非法侵入者 (Undiscovered Trespasser)。

2. 确定义务：

对于未被发现的非法侵入者，农民不负有任何注意义务。即使农民未能培训朋友（过失），或者朋友射击时疏忽大意，由于“义务 (Duty)”这一要素缺失，过失侵权 (Negligence) 的指控无法成立。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (Vicarious Liability)：
虽然农民通常不对朋友的行为负责是正确的，但这并不是本案邻居败诉的根本原因。根本原因是农民对邻居根本没有义务。
选项 C (Negligence)：
此选项试图建立基于“未能提供安全培训”的过失责任。但这只有在农民对邻居负有义务（例如邻居是被许可人）时才成立。由于没有义务，是否存在过失行为就无关紧要了。
选项 D (Strict Liability)：
这是一个常见的陷阱。打猎/使用枪支虽然危险，但在法律上通常不被视为“异常危险活动 (Abnormally Dangerous Activity)”。因此不适用严格责任，仍需证明过失。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

看到 "Landowner Liability" 的题目时，第一步永远是看题目要求适用 "Traditional Rules" 还是 "Modern Trend"。

  • 如果是 Traditional：必须先判断原告身份（Trespasser/Licensee/Invitee）。
  • 如果是 Modern：通常对所有进入者（除公然侵入者外）都负有“合理注意义务 (Reasonable Care)”。

本题明确规定适用 Traditional Rules，因此“身份”是解题的关键。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A fire that started in the defendant's warehouse spread to the plaintiff's adjacent warehouse. The defendant did not intentionally start the fire, and the plaintiff can produce no evidence as to how the fire started. However, the defendant had failed to install a sprinkler system, which was required by a criminal statute. The plaintiff can produce evidence that had the sprinkler system been installed, it could have extinguished the fire before it spread.
In an action by the plaintiff against the defendant to recover for the fire damage, is it possible for the plaintiff to prevail?

choices.A: No, because there is no evidence that the defendant negligently caused the fire to start.
choices.B: No, because the statute provides only for criminal penalties.
choices.C: Yes, because a landowner is strictly liable for harm to others caused by the spread of fire from his premises under the doctrine of Rylands v. Fletcher.
choices.D: Yes, because the plaintiff was harmed as a result of the defendant's violation of a statute that was meant to protect against this type of occurrence.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Elements of negligence per se
• Defendant violated statute or ordinance
• Plaintiff suffered type of harm statute or ordinance was intended to prevent
• Plaintiff is in class of persons statute or ordinance was intended to protect

Civil actions for accidental fire damage are typically based on negligence. To prevail on a negligence claim, the plaintiff must prove the following elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. And under the doctrine of negligence per se, the elements of duty and breach are presumed if:

  • the defendant violated a statute
  • that statute was intended to prevent the type of harm suffered by the plaintiff and
  • the plaintiff is within a class of persons that the statute was intended to protect.

Here, the defendant violated a statute designed to protect buildings and people from fire by failing to install a sprinkler system. As a result, the defendant's duty and breach will be presumed. And though there is no evidence that he negligently caused the fire to start, there is evidence that a sprinkler system could have prevented the fire from spreading to the plaintiff's warehouse (Choice A). As a result, there is evidence that the defendant's failure to install a sprinkler system caused the plaintiff's loss—making it possible for the plaintiff to prevail.

(Choice B) The fact that a statute provides only for criminal penalties does not preclude it from establishing a duty of care for a civil negligence claim.

(Choice C) Under the modern interpretation of Rylands v. Fletcher, a landowner is strictly liable for harm caused by an abnormally dangerous activity on his/her land. Since there is no indication that the defendant was engaging in any such activity in his warehouse here, this precedent does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of negligence per se, duty and breach are presumed if (1) the defendant violated a statute, (2) that statute was intended to prevent the type of harm suffered by the plaintiff, and (3) the plaintiff is within a class of persons that the statute was intended to protect.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 288B (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that it is negligent per se to violate a statute that establishes a duty of care).
  • Rylands v. Fletcher [1868] UKHL 1, [1868] LR 3 (HL) 330 (appeal taken from Eng.) (holding the defendant strictly liable for storing water that flooded the plaintiff's adjacent land).
questions.zh-question:
一场始于被告仓库的火灾蔓延至原告相邻的仓库。被告并非故意纵火，且原告无法提供任何关于火灾起因的证据。然而，被告未能安装刑事法规所要求的自动喷淋系统。原告可以提供证据证明，如果安装了自动喷淋系统，火灾本可以在蔓延前被扑灭。

在原告向被告提起的火灾损害赔偿诉讼中，原告是否有可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为没有证据表明被告因过失导致火灾发生。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该法规仅规定了刑事处罚。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为根据 Rylands v. Fletcher 案的原则，土地所有者对其土地上火灾蔓延对他人造成的损害承担严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为原告所受的损害是被告违反一项旨在防止此类事件发生的法规所导致的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence Per Se
正确答案: 选项 D

原告有可能胜诉，因为原告所受的损害是被告违反一项旨在防止此类事件发生的法规所导致的。

核心考点：法定过失

本题考查的是 Negligence Per Se（法定过失）原则。在普通法中，如果被告违反了某项安全法规（即使是刑事法规），法院可以直接推定被告存在过失（Breach of Duty）。

构成要件 (Elements)：

  • 被告违反了法规 (Statute violated)。
  • 原告属于该法规旨在保护的人群 (Class of persons protected)。
  • 原告遭受的伤害属于该法规旨在防止的类型 (Type of harm to be prevented)。
案情深度解析

1. 义务与违约的推定 (Duty & Breach):
被告违反了要求安装自动喷淋系统（sprinkler system）的刑事法规。

  • 保护对象：相邻的财产所有者（原告）显然属于防火法规保护的人群。
  • 伤害类型：火灾蔓延造成的财产损失正是安装喷淋系统旨在防止的伤害。
因此，根据 Negligence Per Se，被告的“注意义务”和“违约行为”已被确立。

2. 因果关系 (Causation):
虽然被告没有“点火”，但过失侵权不仅包括制造风险，也包括未能采取法律要求的预防措施。题目明确指出：“有证据表明，如果安装了喷淋系统，火灾本可以在蔓延前被扑灭。”这直接建立了事实因果关系 (Causation in fact)。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A (No Negligence in starting):
错误。虽然被告没有过失地“引发”火灾，但他过失地“未能阻止”火灾蔓延（通过违反法规）。侵权责任可以基于不作为（Failure to act），前提是存在法律义务（此处由法规确立）。
选项 B (Criminal Statute):
错误。刑事法规（Criminal Statute）经常被民事法庭用来确立民事诉讼中的注意义务标准（Standard of Care）。法规仅规定刑事处罚并不妨碍其在侵权法中的适用。
选项 C (Rylands v. Fletcher):
错误。Rylands v. Fletcher 确立的是严格责任 (Strict Liability)，适用于“异常危险的活动”（Abnormally Dangerous Activities）。普通的仓库储存通常不被视为异常危险活动，因此不适用严格责任，必须证明过失（本题通过法定过失证明）。
💡 MBE 答题技巧
当题目中出现“违反了法规/条例”（violated a statute/ordinance）时，立即联想 Negligence Per Se。

检查两点： 1. 受害人是不是法规想保护的人？ 2. 发生的事故是不是法规想避免的事？
如果都是 Yes，那么 Duty 和 Breach 就成立了，接下来只需看 Causation（因果关系）。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The owner of a shopping mall hired a construction company to design and construct a new entryway to the mall. The construction company negligently selected an unusually slippery material for the floor covering. A week after the entryway was completed, a customer who had come to the mall to buy cosmetics slipped on the floor of the entryway, sustaining injuries. The customer sued the mall owner for the construction company's negligent design of the mall's entryway.
Will the injured customer be likely to recover damages?

choices.A: No, because no other customers had previously slipped on the floor.
choices.B: No, because the construction company will likely be considered an independent contractor.
choices.C: Yes, because the customer intended to make a purchase at the mall.
choices.D: Yes, because the mall owner's duty to maintain safe conditions was nondelegable.

questions.explanation:
Nondelegable duties
(duties that cannot be assigned to another to avoid liability)

Nondelegable duties
  • Maintain safe conditions on premises open to public (eg, store, restaurant)
  • Safely perform activities that:
    • are abnormally or highly dangerous
    • infringe on private property right (eg, nuisance, trespass)
    • are regulated by law or
    • are conducted in public place

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for torts committed by its independent contractor—one who performs work for another outside an employment relationship. However, vicarious liability will be imposed if the independent contractor's work breaches a nondelegable duty owed by the principal—a duty of care that cannot be assigned to a third party to avoid liability. This includes the duty of a land possessor who holds his/her land open to the public to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

Here, the construction company was likely an independent contractor since it was hired for a one-time job— to design and construct a new entryway to the mall. And though the mall owner ordinarily would not be liable for an independent contractor's torts, the mall owner had a nondelegable duty to maintain safe conditions for its customers (Choice B). Since the construction company's work—selecting a slippery material for the floor—breached that duty, the mall owner is vicariously liable for the customer's resulting injuries.

(Choice A) Proof of prior accidents could help show that the entryway was negligently designed. But such proof is not required here since (1) possessors have a nondelegable duty to use reasonable care to discover dangerous conditions on the land before an injury occurs and (2) the construction company's negligence is stipulated above.

(Choice C) Since the mall was held open to the public, the mall owner had a nondelegable duty to maintain safe premises for all business visitors (eg, window shoppers) not just those intending to make a purchase. Therefore, the customer's intention to make a purchase is irrelevant to her recovery.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for its independent contractor's torts. However, vicarious liability will be imposed when the independent contractor breaches a nondelegable duty of care owed by the principal—eg, a land possessor's duty to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 57 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (no vicarious liability generally for independent contractors).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 344 (nondelegable duty to keep business premises safe).
questions.zh-question:
一家购物中心的所有人聘请了一家建筑公司为该购物中心设计和建造一个新的入口通道。该建筑公司因过失选用了异常湿滑的材料作为地面铺装。入口通道完工一周后，一位前来购物中心购买化妆品的顾客在入口通道的地面上滑倒并受伤。该顾客因建筑公司对购物中心入口通道的过失设计而起诉购物中心所有人。

受伤的顾客是否可能获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为之前没有其他顾客在该地面上滑倒过。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该建筑公司很可能被视为一个独立承包商。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该顾客有意在购物中心进行消费。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为购物中心所有人维持安全状况的义务是不可转委托的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 侵权法考点解析

Negligence & Vicarious Liability
正确答案：D 是的，因为购物中心所有人维持安全状况的义务是不可转委托的。
Yes, because the mall owner's duty to maintain safe conditions was nondelegable.
核心考点：独立承包商与不可转委托义务

一般原则 (General Rule)：
通常情况下，委托人（Principal）不对独立承包商 (Independent Contractor) 的侵权行为承担替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)。这与雇主对雇员的责任不同。

关键例外 (The Exception)：不可转委托的义务 (Nondelegable Duties)
出于公共政策的考量，某些义务非常重要，以至于法律不允许责任人通过雇佣承包商来推卸责任。

本案适用：
土地占有者（如购物中心）向公众开放其场所时，负有保持场所对商业访客 (Business Invitees) 安全的义务。这是一项不可转委托的义务。

案情逻辑分析
  1. 身份认定：建筑公司是一次性受雇完成特定项目，属于独立承包商，而非雇员。
  2. 过失认定：题目已明确指出建筑公司“过失地 (negligently)”选择了湿滑材料。
  3. 责任归属：虽然一般不对独立承包商负责，但由于“保持公共场所安全”是不可转委托的义务，购物中心所有人必须对该不安全状况负责，即使该状况是由承包商造成的。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

选项 A 错误 “没有其他顾客滑倒”：
缺乏过往事故记录并不能免除被告的责任。只要能证明存在不合理的危险状况且被告违反了注意义务即可。题目已定性为“过失设计”，因此不需要过往事故来证明危险性。
选项 B 错误 “建筑公司是独立承包商”：
这是本题最大的陷阱。虽然陈述本身属实（它是独立承包商），但它忽略了“不可转委托义务”这一例外情况。在MBE考试中，当涉及到公共场所安全时，独立承包商身份不能作为业主的免责金牌。
选项 C 错误 “顾客意图消费”：
虽然这证实了顾客是Invitee（受邀人），但理由不够精准。购物中心对所有公众访客（包括只逛不买的人）都负有安全义务。更重要的是，该选项没有触及“为什么业主需要为承包商的过错负责”这一核心法律问题。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

当你看到“业主/店主 (Landowner/Shopkeeper)” + “向公众开放 (Open to public)” + “维修/装修造成伤害 (Injury due to repair/construction)” 的组合时：

  • 第一反应：通常是对独立承包商不负责。
  • 第二反应：马上检查是否有“不可转委托义务”。

公共场所的安全维护几乎总是不可转委托的。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A longshoreman fell to his death through an open hatch on the deck of a ship. The longshoreman was an employee of a company that had contracted with the ship's owner to load and unload the ship. The fall occurred at night, when loading work was over for the day, and there was no reason for the longshoreman to have been near the hatch.
A negligence action was filed against the ship's owner for the death of the longshoreman. In that action, the owner has moved for summary judgment and has provided unrebutted evidence that it is customary for the crews of ships to open the hatches for ventilation after the longshoremen have left the ships.
How should the court respond to the motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion and submit the case to the jury with instructions that the custom is relevant but not conclusive on the issue of negligence.
choices.B: Deny the motion and submit the case to the jury with instructions that the ship's owner should win if the longshoreman was improperly near the hatch.
choices.C: Deny the motion, because the probability of serious injury caused by falling down an open hatch clearly outweighs the burden of keeping the hatch closed.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the custom should be considered conclusive on the issue of negligence.

questions.explanation:
Elements of negligence
  • Duty – defendant owed duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – defendant breached duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – defendant's breach actually and proximately caused plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

To determine whether a defendant was negligent, the trier of fact (eg, the jury) can consider all relevant factors—including whether the defendant complied with community or industry custom. But custom is not conclusive on the issue of negligence since, among other things, the entire community or industry may be negligent. Therefore, this court should deny the ship owner's summary judgment motion and instruct the jury that the custom of opening the hatches after the longshoremen have left the ship is relevant—but not conclusive ((Choice D)).

(Choice B) The fact that the longshoreman was improperly near the hatch could show that he was contributorily negligent—ie, failed to use reasonable care for his own protection. This would completely bar his recovery if the traditional common law rule applied. But under the comparative negligence rule (default rule on the MBE), contributory negligence only reduces recovery. Therefore, the ship's owner cannot win on this basis.

(Choice C) In determining negligence issues, the jury can consider whether the probability of harm outweighed the burden of avoiding that harm (ie, the Hand formula). But here, there is no indication that the probability of serious injury caused by falling down an open hatch outweighs the burden of keeping the hatch closed. This is particularly true since it is customary to only open the hatches after the longshoremen have left the ship.

📌 Educational Objective

Evidence that the defendant complied with (or deviated from) community or industry custom is relevant—but not conclusive—on the issue of negligence.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 295A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that the customs of the community are relevant but not conclusive on the issue of negligence).
questions.zh-question:
一名码头工人在船甲板上从一个敞开的舱口坠落身亡。该码头工人是一家公司的雇员，该公司与船主签订了装卸船只的合同。坠落事件发生在晚上，当时当天的装货工作已经结束，码头工人没有理由靠近该舱口。

就该码头工人的死亡，已向船主提起过失诉讼。在该诉讼中，船主已提出简易判决动议，并提供了无可辩驳的证据，证明船员在码头工人离开船只后打开舱口通风是惯例。

法院应如何回应此动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，并将案件提交给陪审团，并指示陪审团该惯例与过失问题相关，但并非决定性因素。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，并将案件提交给陪审团，并指示陪审团如果码头工人不当靠近舱口，则船主应胜诉。
zh-choices.C: 驳回动议，因为从敞开的舱口坠落造成严重伤害的可能性明显超过了保持舱口关闭的负担。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为该惯例应被视为过失问题上的决定性因素。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence & Custom

本题考察的是侵权法中行业惯例（Custom/Industry Practice）在认定过失（Negligence）时的法律效力。

核心考点：惯例的证据效力 在过失侵权案件中，被告是否遵守了行业惯例是相关证据（Relevant Evidence），但绝非决定性证据（Conclusive Evidence）。

"Custom is relevant, but not conclusive."
法律逻辑解析

1. 惯例 ≠ 合理注意义务标准
即使整个行业都遵循某种做法（如本题中“工人离开后打开舱口通风”），这并不意味着该做法本身是合理的。如果整个行业都为了省钱或省事而采取不安全的做法，那么整个行业都可能存在过失。

2. 著名的 T.J. Hooper 规则
这一原则源自著名的 The T.J. Hooper 案。法官 Learned Hand 指出，法院不能让行业自己设定法律标准，否则行业可能会设定过低的标准。

3. 陪审团的角色
本案中，船主虽然证明了这是惯例，但原告仍可以主张：尽管是惯例，但在夜间无人看管时敞开舱口且没有防护措施是不合理的（Unreasonable）。这是一个事实问题，必须交给陪审团（Jury）去权衡，而不能由法官通过简易判决（Summary Judgment）直接裁定。

选项深度剖析
正确选项 A 驳回动议，提交陪审团。
法院应驳回船主的简易判决申请。法官应指示陪审团：可以将“惯例”作为考量被告是否尽到合理注意义务的因素之一，但不能直接因为被告遵守了惯例就判定其无过失。
错误选项 D 批准动议，视为决定性因素。
这是本题最大的陷阱。MBE 经常测试这一点：遵守惯例从来不是过失问题的“免死金牌”（Conclusive）。
错误选项 B 关于受害者的位置。
这涉及共同过失（Contributory/Comparative Negligence）。即使受害者有过错，在现代比较过失制度下，这通常只是减少赔偿金额，而不是让被告直接胜诉（除非是极少数适用严格共同过失的辖区，但MBE默认适用比较过失）。更重要的是，这属于事实争议，不能作为简易判决的依据。
💡MBE 答题技巧
看到题目中出现“Custom”（惯例）、“Industry Standard”（行业标准）时，脑海中要立刻浮现这句话：
"Floor, not a ceiling."

如果选项说惯例是 "Conclusive"（决定性的）或者 "Complete defense"（完全抗辩），该选项通常是错误的。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man shared an apartment with his roommate in a crowded multistory apartment building. One late night, the man fell asleep in bed while smoking a cigarette. The cigarette fell onto the rug, which subsequently caught fire. The man woke up and fled the building, forgetting to wake up his roommate. As the rest of the apartment quickly caught fire, the roommate woke up. He first tried to extinguish the fire, and when that failed, he tried to escape. By that time, fire alarms had been set off throughout the building. Many tenants were panicking and running out of the apartment building as quickly as possible. In the chaos, the roommate was trampled by another tenant as they both tried to exit the building. The roommate sustained severe smoke inhalation injuries when he tried to extinguish the fire. Because of the roommate's undisclosed preexisting lung condition, the damage caused a lung infection requiring a month of costly in-patient care at a hospital. The roommate also suffered a broken arm when he was trampled by the other tenant.
If the roommate sues the man for negligence, for what injuries will the man be required to pay damages?

choices.A: No injuries, because there is no proper direct causal link between the man's negligence and the roommate's injuries.
choices.B: Only the lung infection, because the panicked escape of the other tenant was an unforeseeable intervening cause of the roommate's broken arm.
choices.C: Only the broken arm, because the man could not have predicted the extent of the roommate's injuries from the smoke.
choices.D: Both the lung infection and the broken arm, because the man's negligence was the factual and proximate cause of both injuries.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Relevance of foreseeability for negligence
Duty • Defendant's duty only extends to foreseeable risks of his/her conduct
Breach • Defendant fails to act like reasonable person under similar circumstances by not mitigating foreseeable risks
Causation • Actual (but for) cause - foreseeability irrelevant
• Proximate cause - plaintiff's harm must have been foreseeable consequence of defendant's breach
Damages • Foreseeability irrelevant (ie, eggshell-skull rule)

Negligence has four elements (see table above), including causation. To prove causation, the plaintiff must show that the defendant was the actual (e.g., factual) and proximate cause of the plaintiff's injuries.

Proximate cause requires the plaintiff to show that the plaintiff's harm was a reasonably foreseeable consequence of the defendant's conduct. Unforeseeable intervening acts (i.e., superseding causes) break the chain of causation, but negligent intervening acts are typically considered foreseeable and do not.

Here, the roommate suffered a broken arm and a severe lung infection because of the man's negligence in starting the fire. Injuries such as smoke inhalation are a reasonably foreseeable consequence of fire. And though another tenant caused the roommate's broken arm (negligent intervening act), it is foreseeable that a fire would cause other tenants of the multi-story apartment building to panic and try to escape. This means that there is a proper causal link between the man's negligence and both of the roommate's injuries. (Choices A and B)

Once causation is established, the plaintiff may recover damages for any physical injury and emotional distress resulting from the defendant's negligence. And under the eggshell-plaintiff rule (i.e., thin-skull rule), the defendant need not have foreseen the extent of damages to be subject to liability for all damages.

Here, the man could not have predicted the extent of the roommate's injuries from the smoke, as he was unaware of the roommate's preexisting lung condition. But the man need not have foreseen the extent of the damages resulting from his negligence ((Choice C)). Therefore, if the roommate sues the man for negligence, the man will be required to pay damages for both the lung infection and the broken arm because his negligence was the factual and proximate cause of both.

📌 Educational Objective

Negligence requires proof that the defendant's breach of duty was the actual and proximate cause of the plaintiff's harm. And under the eggshell-plaintiff rule (i.e., thin-skull rule), the defendant is subject to liability for all resulting damages—even those that were not foreseeable.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 435 (Am. L. Inst. 1965) (explaining that a tortfeasor can be liable for harm that he/she neither foresaw nor should have foreseen).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical & Emotional Harm § 31 (Am. L. Inst. 2010) (setting forth the thin-skull rule).

一名男子与其室友合住在一栋拥挤的多层公寓楼里。一天深夜，这名男子躺在床上抽烟时睡着了。香烟掉到地毯上，随后引发火灾。男子醒来后逃离大楼，却忘了叫醒室友。随着公寓其余部分迅速起火，室友醒了过来。他先试图扑灭火灾，但未能成功，于是尝试逃生。到那时，整栋楼里都已经响起了火警报警器。许多住户惊慌失措，争相尽快跑出公寓楼。在混乱中，室友与另一名住户同时试图离开大楼时被对方踩踏。室友在试图扑灭火灾时还遭受了严重的 smoke inhalation injuries（吸入浓烟损伤）。由于室友未披露的既往肺部疾病，这种损伤导致肺部感染，需要在医院进行为期一个月且费用高昂的住院治疗。室友还在被另一名住户踩踏时摔断了胳膊。
如果室友以 negligence（过失）起诉该男子，男子需要就哪些损害承担赔偿责任？

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man decided to have lunch at a new restaurant. While the man was eating his lunch, an accidental fire broke out in the kitchen, and the dining room quickly filled with smoke. The other restaurant patrons experienced mild discomfort, which did not require medical treatment. However, the man had been born with an acute and discerning sense of smell, and he had a job as a senior perfumer at a fragrance corporation. He subsequently sued the restaurant in negligence for the injury to the olfactory sensory cells in his nasal cavity that left him unable to work. His annual salary had been $250,000 before the accident.
Assuming that the man can otherwise establish the elements of negligence, can he recover damages for the injury to his olfactory sensory cells as well as for his loss of employment?

choices.A: No, because economic damages due to loss of employment are not recoverable in a negligence action.
choices.B: No, because the man's acute and discerning sense of smell was a preexisting condition.
choices.C: Yes, because the man can recover even if the extent of his injuries was not reasonably foreseeable.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's damages were severe and exceeded those of the other restaurant patrons.

questions.explanation:
Recovery of compensatory damages
(initial harm + normal consequences)
Initial physical harm
Subsequent physical harm
Subsequent economic harm
Subsequent emotional harm

A successful negligence claim requires proof that the plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, personal injury or property damage) as a result of the defendant's negligent conduct. Assuming all other elements are proved, the plaintiff can then recover compensatory damages for his/her initial physical harm AND any subsequent harm (physical, economic, or emotional) that is traceable to that initial harm. This is true even if the extent of the harm was unusual or unforeseeable because "the defendant takes the victim as found."

Here, the man suffered injuries to his olfactory sensory cells (initial physical harm) as a result of the fire. This left the man unable to perform his job as a senior perfume tester (economic harm traceable to initial harm). Therefore, the man can recover compensatory damages for the injury to his olfactory sensory cells as well as for his lost employment—even if the extent of his injuries was not reasonably foreseeable.

*This is known colloquially as the "thin-skull" or "eggshell plaintiff" rule.

(Choice A) A plaintiff who suffers economic damages (eg, due to loss of employment) without any related personal injury or property damage cannot recover in a negligence action. But economic damages stemming from physical harm (as seen here) are recoverable.

(Choice B) The physical harm required for negligence includes the exacerbation of a preexisting condition, so the fact that the man's acute and discerning sense of smell was a preexisting condition does not defeat his claim.

(Choice D) While a negligence plaintiff must prove actual damages, the damages need not be severe or exceed those suffered by others who did not have a preexisting condition.

📌 Educational Objective

A successful negligence plaintiff can recover compensatory damages for his/her initial physical harm as well as any subsequent harm (physical, economic, or emotional) that stems from that initial harm. This is so even if the extent of the harm was unusual or unforeseeable.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 31 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (preexisting conditions and unforeseeable harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定去一家新餐厅吃午饭。该男子在用餐时，厨房意外起火，餐厅迅速充满了烟雾。其他餐厅的顾客感到了轻微不适，但无需医疗。然而，该男子天生嗅觉敏锐，他在一家香水公司担任高级调香师。他随后以negligence（过失）为由起诉该餐厅，诉称其鼻腔嗅觉感觉细胞受损，导致他无法工作。事故发生前，他的年薪为25万美元。

假设该男子能够证明negligence（过失）的所有要素，他是否可以就其嗅觉感觉细胞的损伤以及失业损失获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为在negligence（过失）诉讼中，因失业造成的经济损失是不可获赔的。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该男子敏锐的嗅觉是其既存状况。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为即使其伤害程度并非合理可预见，该男子仍然可以获得赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该男子的损害严重，并超过了其他餐厅顾客的损害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts / Negligence
核心考点：蛋壳原告规则
本题考查的是侵权法中著名的 "Eggshell Plaintiff Rule"（蛋壳原告规则），也被称为 "Thin Skull Rule"。

法律原则：
"The defendant takes the victim as he finds him."
（被告必须接受受害者的现状。）
案情逻辑推演

1. 过失成立： 题目已假设男子能证明 Negligence 的所有要素（Duty, Breach, Causation, Damages）。
2. 初始伤害： 餐厅火灾导致男子嗅觉细胞受损（Physical Harm）。
3. 特殊体质： 男子是高级调香师，嗅觉极其敏锐且对其职业至关重要。
4. 后果： 尽管普通人只感到轻微不适，但该男子遭受了严重的职业生涯打击和巨额经济损失。

选项深度解析
正确答案 C 理由： 根据 Eggshell Plaintiff Rule，一旦被告的过失行为造成了原告的身体伤害（Physical Harm），被告必须对所有由此产生的后果负责。

即使伤害的程度 (Extent) 是不可预见的（Unforeseeable），被告仍需全额赔偿。在本案中，虽然餐厅无法预见顾客是调香师，但既然造成了身体伤害，就必须赔偿由此导致的失业损失。
选项 A 错误 虽然纯粹的经济损失（Pure Economic Loss）通常不可赔偿，但本案中的经济损失是附带于身体伤害（Parasitic to physical injury）的。因为嗅觉细胞受损（身体伤害）导致了无法工作，所以这部分经济损失是可以追偿的。
选项 B 错误 这恰恰是蛋壳原告规则保护的情况。原告的既存状况（Preexisting Condition，即敏锐的嗅觉）并不能成为被告免责的理由。被告必须对加重或引发的后果负责。
选项 D 错误 逻辑重心错误。原告获赔不是因为他的损失“比别人严重”，而是因为根据法律规则，被告必须对受害者的实际损失负责。比较其他顾客的损失并不是判断被告是否承担责任的法律标准。
💡 MBE 考试通关秘籍 在 Negligence 题目中，区分 "Type of Harm"（伤害类型）和 "Extent of Harm"（伤害程度）：
  • 伤害类型：必须是可预见的（Foreseeable）。例如，火灾导致烟雾吸入是可预见的。
  • 伤害程度：不需要是可预见的。只要造成了伤害，哪怕原告是“玻璃做的”，被告也要赔到底。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A child was bitten by a dog while playing in a fenced-in common area of an apartment complex owned by a landlord. The child was the guest of a tenant living in the complex, and the dog was owned by another tenant. The owner of the dog knew that the dog had a propensity to bite, but the landlord did not have any notice of the dog's vicious propensities.
In an action by the child against the landlord, will the child be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because a landlord owes no duty to a tenant's guests.
choices.B: No, because the landlord did not have notice of the dog's vicious propensities.
choices.C: Yes, because a landlord's duty to protect a tenant's guests from dangerous conditions is nondelegable.
choices.D: Yes, because in these circumstances a landlord is strictly liable.

questions.explanation:
Dangerous conditions on land
(landlord's duties)
  • Warn tenant of known latent (hidden) defects on land
  • Safely perform repairs
  • Ensure common areas are in safe condition
  • Maintain areas necessary for safe use of land (eg, walls, roof)
  • Keep land in good repair (lease provision required)
  • Protect entrants from dangerous condition on land leased for public purpose

Landlords are generally not liable for harm that occurs on the leased premises. This is because they give up possession and control of the premises to their tenants and are unlikely to be aware of subsequent dangers. However, landlords owe tenants and other foreseeable persons on the premises (eg, their guests) a duty to use reasonable care to ensure the safety of common areas that remain under the landlord's control (Choice A). A landlord who breaches this duty and causes the plaintiff physical harm is liable for negligence.

Here, the child's presence in the apartment complex was foreseeable since he was a tenant's guest. The child was then bitten by another tenant's dog in a common area of the apartment complex. As a result, the landlord owed the child a duty of reasonable care. But since the landlord had no reason to know that the dog posed a risk to those on his property, his failure to take precautions against that risk did not breach this duty of care. Therefore, the child is unlikely to prevail in an action against the landlord.

(Choice C) Landlords owe tenants and their guests a nondelgable duty to protect them from dangerous physical conditions on the property that remain under the landlord's control (eg, broken elevators). But a vicious dog is not such a condition. Additionally, it does not matter whether the landlord's duty was nondelegable here since there is no evidence that he assigned its performance to a third party whose negligence caused the child's injuries.

(Choice D) Strict liability for harm caused by a dog (or other animal) with vicious propensities extends to the dog's owners or possessors who know or should know of that propensitity. But since the landlord neither owned nor possessed the dog, strict liability is inapplicable.

📌 Educational Objective

Landlords owe foreseeable persons on the leased premises (eg, tenants and their guests) a duty to use reasonable care to ensure the safety of common areas that remain under the landlord's control.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 53 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (lessor's duties).
questions.zh-question:
一名儿童在房东拥有的一处公寓大楼的围栏公共区域玩耍时，被一只狗咬伤。该儿童是居住在该大楼内一名租户的客人，而狗则为另一名租户所有。狗的主人知道该狗有咬人倾向，但房东对该狗的凶猛倾向并未收到任何通知。

在该儿童对房东提起的诉讼中，该儿童是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为房东对租户的客人不负有任何义务。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为房东未曾被告知该狗的凶猛倾向。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为房东保护租户的客人免受危险状况侵害的义务是不可转委托的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为在此情况下，房东应承担严格责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 房东过失责任
正确答案 B 核心逻辑：知情 (Notice)

本题的关键在于过失 (Negligence) 的构成要件。虽然房东对公共区域负有注意义务，但要认定房东违背了该义务，房东必须对危险状况知情 (Notice)。

题目明确指出房东对狗的凶猛倾向“没有任何通知” (did not have any notice)。如果没有知情，房东就无法预见伤害，因此没有违反注意义务。

⚖️ 法律规则详解

1. 房东的一般义务 (Landlord's Duty)：
通常情况下，房东对租户及其客人在租赁物业内受到的伤害不承担责任。但是，对于房东保留控制权的公共区域 (Common Areas)（如大厅、走廊、围栏内的院子），房东有义务行使合理的注意 (Reasonable Care) 以维护其安全。

2. 针对动物的责任 (Liability for Animals)：
如果伤害是由租户的动物造成的，房东要承担过失责任必须同时满足以下条件：

  • 房东对发生伤害的区域有控制权（本题满足，是公共区域）；
  • 房东实际知晓或理应知晓 (Actual or Constructive Knowledge) 该动物具有危险倾向；
  • 房东有能力移除该危险（例如驱逐租户或移除动物）。
避坑指南 为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 A 错误： 房东对租户的客人（Guests）确实负有义务。在公共区域，客人通常被视为被许可人 (Licensees) 或 受邀人 (Invitees)（取决于司法管辖区），房东对其负有合理注意义务。说“没有义务”是法律上的错误。
  • 选项 C 错误： 虽然房东维护公共区域（如修缮楼梯）的义务通常是不可转委托的 (Nondelegable)，但这并不意味着房东对所有发生的事故都自动负责。不可转委托义务仍需建立在房东有过失（即知晓危险却未处理）的基础上。此外，狗不是“物理状况” (Physical Condition)。
  • 选项 D 错误： 严格责任 (Strict Liability) 适用于明知动物有危险倾向的拥有者 (Owner) 或 占有人 (Possessor)。房东既不是狗的主人也不是占有人，因此不承担严格责任，只承担过失责任。
🎓 MBE 实战技巧

在处理涉及第三方行为 (Third-party acts) 或 动物 (Animals) 的房东责任问题时，请遵循以下思维路径：

  1. 位置： 事故是否发生在公共区域？（如果是，房东有义务）。
  2. 知情 (Notice)： 房东是否知道这个特定的危险？（这是最常见的考点）。

如果题目明确说房东“不知道” (did not have notice)，那么在过失 (Negligence) 诉讼中，房东通常会胜诉。

MBE Negligence Q83135 Analysis
Designed for Mobile Learning

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An elderly neighbor hired a 17-year-old boy with a reputation for reckless driving to drive the neighbor on errands once a week. One day the teenager, driving the neighbor's car, took the neighbor to the grocery store. While the neighbor was in the store, the teenager drove out of the parking lot and headed for a party on the other side of town. While on his way to the party, the teenager negligently turned in front of a moving car and caused a collision. The other driver was injured in the collision.
The injured driver has brought an action for damages against the neighbor, based on negligent entrustment, and against the teenager. The jury has found that the injured driver's damages were $100,000, that the injured driver was 10% at fault, that the teenager was 60% at fault, and that the neighbor was 30% at fault for entrusting his car to the teenager.
Based on these damage and responsibility amounts, what is the maximum that the injured driver could recover from the neighbor?
questions.explanation:
Explanation
Negligence rules of recovery

To determine the amount of compensatory damages a plaintiff may recover in a negligence action, the following rules apply (unless the question otherwise indicates):

  • Pure comparative negligence – when the plaintiff's own negligence contributes to his/her harm, the plaintiff's recovery is reduced by his/her proportionate share of fault
  • Joint and several liability – when multiple defendants cause the plaintiff indivisible harm, the plaintiff can recover the total amount of damages from any defendant (who can then sue the others for contribution)

Here, the jury determined that the injured driver sustained $100,000 in damages and apportioned liability as follows: the driver (10%), the neighbor (30%), and the teenager (60%). The driver's recovery will be reduced by his proportionate share of fault ($100,000 - $10,000 = $90,000) (Choice B). The driver may then recover the $90,000 from any of the defendants, including the neighbor.*

*The neighbor could then bring a contribution action against the teenager for $60,000—the amount attributable to the teenager's fault.

(Choices C & D) Had the jurisdiction adopted several liability (not seen here), each defendant would have been liable only for his/her proportionate share of fault. This would mean that the driver could only recover $30,000 from the neighbor for negligently entrusting his car and $60,000 from the teenager for his negligent driving (as opposed to recovering the full $90,000 from either defendant).

📌 Educational Objective

Under pure comparative negligence, a negligent plaintiff's recovery is reduced by his/her proportionate share of fault. And if multiple defendants cause the plaintiff indivisible harm, joint and several liability allows the plaintiff to recover the total amount of recoverable damages from any defendant.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § 7 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (pure comparative negligence).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § 10 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (joint and several liability).
questions.zh-question:
一位年长的邻居雇佣了一名以鲁莽驾驶而闻名的17岁男孩，每周一次开车为他处理杂事。一天，这名少年驾驶邻居的汽车，载邻居去杂货店。当邻居在店内时，该少年驾车驶出停车场，前往城镇另一边的派对。在去派对的路上，该少年因过失在一个行驶中的车辆前转弯，引发了一场碰撞。另一名驾驶员在碰撞中受伤。

受伤的驾驶员以“过失委托”(negligent entrustment)为由，对邻居和该少年提起了损害赔偿诉讼。陪审团裁定，受伤驾驶员的损失为100,000美元，受伤驾驶员有10%的过错，少年有60%的过错，而邻居因将车委托给该少年而有30%的过错。

基于这些损失和责任金额，受伤驾驶员最多可以从邻居那里获得多少赔偿？
questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence & Joint Liability

✅ 正确答案：B ($90,000)

本题考察的是多方被告情况下的损害赔偿计算，核心在于结合比较过失与连带责任。

🧮 第一步：计算原告可追偿金额

首先，应用纯粹比较过失原则 (Pure Comparative Negligence)。MBE 默认适用此规则，除非题目另有说明。

规则：原告的总赔偿额需扣除其自身过错的比例。
原告过错 10%
(不可追偿) 可追偿部分 90%
($90,000)
$100,000 × (100% - 10%) = $90,000

因此，原告最多可以获得 $90,000 的赔偿。

⚖️ 第二步：谁来赔这笔钱？

这是本题的关键陷阱。虽然陪审团认定邻居只有 30% 的过错，但在 MBE 考试中，对于造成不可分割伤害 (Indivisible Harm) 的多个被告，默认适用连带责任 (Joint and Several Liability)。

  • 连带责任 (Joint and Several Liability): 原告可以向任何一个负有责任的被告索赔全部可追偿金额。
  • 分别责任 (Several Liability): 被告仅按其过错比例赔偿（本题不适用，除非明确指出）。
结论： 原告可以选择向邻居索赔全额的 $90,000。邻居支付后，可以再向少年提起分担诉讼 (Contribution Action) 来追回多付的部分，但这不影响原告的权利。
🎓 考试策略与陷阱排除

为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 A ($100,000): 忽略了原告自己的 10% 过错。比较过失原则下，原告必须承担自己的责任份额。
  • 选项 C ($60,000): 这是少年 (Teenager) 的过错比例份额，或者是误解了计算方式。
  • 选项 D ($30,000): 这是邻居 (Neighbor) 的过错比例份额 ($100k × 30%)。只有在适用“分别责任” (Several Liability) 的辖区才选这个。MBE 默认规则是连带责任。

MBE 黄金法则：

  1. 看到多名被告 + 单一伤害 → 默认想 Joint and Several Liability。
  2. 看到原告有过错 → 先扣除原告的份额，算出 Recoverable Damages。
  3. 题目问 "Maximum recovery from X" → 答案通常是全部可追偿金额（不只是 X 的份额）。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A homeowner was injured when he slipped and fell in a puddle of water on his sunroom floor; the water had accumulated on the floor during a rainstorm because of leaks in the roof. The roof's manufacturer had supplied nondefective materials to the installer, who was a franchisee (and not an employee) of the manufacturer. The leaks resulted from the carelessness of the installer during the installation of the roof.
The installer's truck, which had been parked in front of the homeowner's house during the roof installation, bore the manufacturer's logo. The manufacturer was aware that the truck and the literature supplied by the installer both displayed the manufacturer's logo.
Is there any basis for a claim by the homeowner against the manufacturer?

choices.A: No, because a franchisor has no duty to supervise the conduct of a franchisee.
choices.B: No, under the rule that a manufacturer is liable only for defects in a product that existed at the time the product left the hands of the manufacturer.
choices.C: Yes, because the installer was a franchisee of the manufacturer.
choices.D: Yes, under the rule of apparent agency.

questions.explanation:
A defendant may be vicariously liable for a third party's torts if an agency relationship existed between them—ie, when the third party agreed to act on the defendant's behalf and subject to the defendant's control. Since a franchisor does not control a franchisee's day-to-day operations (no agency relationship), the franchisor is generally not vicariously liable for the franchisee's torts. But under the rule of apparent agency, (ie, apparent authority), vicarious liability can be imposed if:

• the plaintiff reasonably believed that the third party was acting within the scope of an agency relationship with the defendant and
• that belief was traceable to the defendant's manifestations (ie, words or conduct).

Here, the manufacturer (franchisor) would generally not be vicariously liable for the installer's (franchisee's) conduct (Choice C). But the homeowner could have reasonably believed that the installer was acting as the manufacturer's agent since the installer’s truck and literature displayed the manufacturer's logo. And since the manufacturer knew about this and permitted the installer to do so, that belief was traceable to the manufacturer's manifestations. Therefore, the homeowner has a basis for a claim against the manufacturer under the rule of apparent agency.

(Choice A) Although a franchisor is not directly liable for a franchisee's conduct (since the franchisor has no duty to supervise the franchisee), a franchisor can still be vicariously liable for a franchisee's torts under the rule of apparent agency.

(Choice B) Under strict products liability, a manufacturer is only liable for product defects that existed when the product left the manufacturer's hands. Here, the manufacturer supplied nondefective materials to the installer so there is no basis for a strict products liability claim.

(Choice C) Yes, because the installer was a franchisee of the manufacturer.

(Choice D) Yes, under the rule of apparent agency.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the rule of apparent agency, a defendant may be vicariously liable for a third party's torts if (1) the plaintiff reasonably believed that the third party was acting within the scope of an agency relationship with the defendant and (2) that belief was traceable to the defendant's manifestations.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency § 1.01 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (definition of agency).
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency § 2.03 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (apparent agency).
questions.zh-question:
一名房主因在其阳光房地板上的一滩水中滑倒而受伤；这滩水是由于屋顶漏水，在暴雨期间积聚在地板上的。屋顶制造商向安装工提供了无缺陷的材料，该安装工是制造商的特许经营商（而非雇员）。漏水是由于安装工在安装屋顶过程中的疏忽造成的。

在安装屋顶期间，停在房主房前的安装工卡车上带有制造商的标志。制造商知晓该卡车和安装工提供的宣传资料均展示了制造商的标志。

房主向制造商提出索赔是否有任何依据？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为特许人没有义务监督特许经营人的行为。
zh-choices.B: 否，根据规则，制造商仅对产品离开其手时已存在的产品缺陷承担责任。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为安装工是制造商的特许经营人。
zh-choices.D: 是，根据表见代理规则。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 侵权法考点解析

Torts: Vicarious Liability & Agency
D
正确答案：
是，根据表见代理规则。
Yes, under the rule of apparent agency.
核心法律规则：表见代理

一般原则：通常情况下，委托人（Principal）不对独立合同工（Independent Contractor，如特许经营人）的侵权行为承担转承责任（Vicarious Liability）。

例外情况 - 表见代理 (Apparent Agency)：如果委托人通过言行创造出一种代理关系存在的表象，且第三方合理信赖了这种表象，委托人可能需要承担责任。

本案逻辑推演
1. 事实认定 (Fact Pattern)：
安装工是特许经营人（Franchisee），属于独立合同工。通常制造商不对其疏忽负责。
2. 关键细节 (The "Holding Out")：
安装工的卡车和宣传资料上印有制造商的标志（Logo）。制造商知情并允许这种行为。
3. 法律适用 (Application)：
制造商允许安装工使用其品牌标志，这向外界（房主）传达了安装工是其代理人的表象（Manifestation）。房主据此认为安装工代表制造商，这种信赖是合理的。
4. 结论 (Conclusion)：
尽管实际上双方是特许经营关系，但由于满足了“表见代理”的要件，制造商需承担转承责任。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误
虽然特许人通常无义务监督特许经营人，但这忽略了表见代理这一例外情况。本题考查的正是这个例外。
选项 B 错误
这是严格产品责任 (Strict Products Liability) 的抗辩理由。但本案中材料是“无缺陷”的 (nondefective)，问题出在安装服务（疏忽）上，因此不适用产品责任规则。
选项 C 错误
仅仅因为是“特许经营人”并不是承担责任的理由。相反，特许经营人通常被视为独立合同工，这本应是免除制造商责任的理由。制造商承担责任是因为“表见代理”，而不是因为合同关系本身。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在 Torts 题目中，如果看到大公司（医院、连锁店、制造商）和独立合同工（医生、特许经营店）的关系：

  • 首先判断是否为独立合同工 (Independent Contractor)。
  • 如果是，寻找“表见代理” (Apparent Agency) 的线索：统一的制服、Logo、广告宣传、或者原告是否依赖了品牌的声誉。
  • 如果存在这些“对外宣称” (Holding out) 的行为，大公司通常跑不掉。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A woman signed up for a bowling class. Before allowing the woman to bowl, the instructor required her to sign a waiver explicitly stating that she assumed all risk of injuries that she might suffer in connection with the class, including injuries due to negligence or any other fault. After she signed the waiver, the woman was injured when the instructor negligently dropped a bowling ball on the woman's foot.
The woman brought a negligence action against the instructor. The instructor has filed a motion for summary judgment based on the waiver.
What is the woman's best argument in opposition to the instructor's motion?

choices.A: Bowling is an inherently dangerous activity.
choices.B: In circumstances like these, it is against public policy to enforce agreements that insulate people from the consequences of their own negligence.
choices.C: It was unreasonable to require the woman to sign the waiver before she was allowed to bowl.
choices.D: When she signed the form, the woman could not foresee that the instructor would drop a bowling ball on her foot.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Assumption of risk
(tort defense)
ApplicabilityPublic policy limitations
ExpressPlaintiff assented to liability waiver intended to cover type of conduct that caused plaintiff's harmNot a defense when defendant:
• is plaintiff's employer
• is a hotel or common carrier
• is a public servant/service
• has substantially more bargaining power
ImpliedPlaintiff voluntarily accepted known risk of harmNot a defense when plaintiff:
• suffered intentional harm
• is member of statutorily protected class

A person can assume the risk of another's tortious conduct by expressly waiving the right to sue. Such waivers are generally valid if the plaintiff assented (eg, by signing the waiver) AND the waiver was intended to cover the type of conduct that caused the plaintiff's harm. But liability waivers are invalid and cannot justify summary judgment if they are against public policy--ie, when the defendant (1) is the plaintiff's employer, (2) is a hotel or common carrier, (3) is a public servant or service, or (4) has substantially more bargaining power.

Here, the woman signed a waiver assuming all risk of injuries that she might suffer in connection with a bowling class. Since this waiver included injuries caused by negligence or any other fault, it was intended to cover the instructor's negligence in dropping a ball on the woman's foot. But the woman can still oppose the instructor's motion for summary judgment by arguing that it is against public policy to enforce the waiver in circumstances like these--eg, due to a substantial imbalance in bargaining power.

(Choice A) Bowling is not inherently dangerous since it rarely results in serious injuries. And even if bowling were inherently dangerous, this would be irrelevant to whether the waiver violates public policy.

(Choice C) In determining the validity of liability waivers, courts will consider whether the defendant had significantly more bargaining power than the plaintiff--but not the reasonableness of requiring the plaintiff to sign the waiver.

(Choice D) The woman assumed all risk of injuries, including unforeseeable risks. Therefore, the validity of the waiver does not depend on whether the woman could foresee that the instructor would drop a ball on her foot.

📌 Educational Objective

A person can expressly waive the right to sue over another person's tortious conduct. Such waivers are generally valid unless they violate public policy--ie, when the defendant (1) is the plaintiff's employer, (2) is a hotel or common carrier, (3) is a public servant or service, or (4) has substantially more bargaining power.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 496B cmts. c-d (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a person can expressly assume the risk of another's negligence unless the waiver is against public policy).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子报名参加保龄球课程。在允许该女子打保龄球之前，教练要求她签署一份弃权声明，明确表示她承担在课程中可能遭受的所有伤害风险，包括因疏忽或任何其他过失造成的伤害。

签署弃权声明后，该女子因教练疏忽将保龄球掉到她的脚上而受伤。

该女子对教练提起了疏忽之诉。教练基于该弃权声明，提出了即决判决（summary judgment）的动议。

该女子反对教练动议的最佳论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 保龄球是一项内在危险的活动。
zh-choices.B: 在此类情况下，强制执行免除个人自身疏忽责任的协议，是违反公共政策的。
zh-choices.C: 在允许该女子打保龄球之前要求她签署弃权声明是不合理的。
zh-choices.D: 当她签署表格时，该女子无法预见教练会把保龄球掉在她的脚上。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Negligence & Exculpatory Clauses

核心考点
明示风险自负 (Express Assumption of Risk)

在侵权法中，如果原告签署了免责条款 (Exculpatory Clause) 或弃权声明 (Waiver)，明确同意免除被告因疏忽 (Negligence) 造成的责任，这通常构成“明示风险自负”。

一般原则：此类条款通常是有效的，可以作为被告申请即决判决 (Summary Judgment) 的依据。

为什么选 B？

题目问的是原告反对即决判决的最佳论点。

虽然免责条款通常有效，但它们有一个主要的“克星”：公共政策 (Public Policy)。

如果原告能证明该免责条款违反了公共政策，法院就不会执行它。违反公共政策的情况通常包括：

  • 涉及故意侵权或重大过失 (Gross Negligence)；
  • 涉及必要的公共服务（如医疗、公共交通）；
  • 双方议价能力极度不平等 (Gross disparity in bargaining power)。

逻辑链条：尽管对于保龄球这种娱乐活动，法院很可能最终会支持免责条款，但在所有选项中，只有 B 选项提出了一个法律上认可的、能使合同无效的理由（即违反公共政策）。这是原告唯一可行的法律路径。

其他选项为何错误？
选项 A 保龄球是内在危险活动：
首先，保龄球在法律上不被视为“内在危险” (Inherently Dangerous)。其次，即使它是危险的，这反而加强了“风险自负”的理由，而不是推翻免责条款的理由。
选项 C 要求签字是不合理的：
这是一个外行人的论点。在法律上，商家要求顾客签署免责声明作为参与活动的条件是标准商业行为，本身并不构成“不合理” (Unreasonable) 到足以使合同无效。
选项 D 无法预见具体伤害：
免责条款明确覆盖了“疏忽” (Negligence)。疏忽的本质就是意外。只要原告同意免除“疏忽”责任，她不需要预见到具体的事故发生方式（如球掉在脚上）。她已经承担了“所有”与课程相关的风险。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

当题目涉及合同免责条款 (Waiver/Release) 时，请记住：

  1. 默认有效：对于普通疏忽 (Ordinary Negligence)，免责条款通常有效。
  2. 攻击点：要推翻它，必须寻找公共政策 (Public Policy) 理由（如故意行为、公共利益、议价能力悬殊）。
  3. 排除法：不要被“不公平”或“没想到”这种非法律术语迷惑。寻找最扎实的法律抗辩理由。

B.text: insulate people from the consequences of their own negligence

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A quarterback and a linebacker were competing against one another in a professional football game. At one point during the game, the quarterback attempted to throw the football to one of his teammates. At the same time, the linebacker was chasing the quarterback in order to tackle him before the ball could be thrown. Just as the linebacker was about to tackle the quarterback, the referee blew her whistle, indicating that the play was over and that the players should stop what they were doing. Nevertheless, the linebacker tackled the quarterback two seconds after the whistle was blown and broke the quarterback's arm.
If the quarterback files a negligence action against the linebacker, will the quarterback be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the linebacker did not intend to break the quarterback's arm.
choices.B: No, because the quarterback assumed the risk of breaking his arm by playing football.
choices.C: Yes, because the linebacker breached the duty of care he owed to the quarterback.
choices.D: Yes, because the linebacker tackled the quarterback after the referee blew the whistle.

questions.explanation:
Assumption of risk
(tort defense)
Applicability Public policy limitations
Express Plaintiff assented to liability waiver intended to cover type of conduct that caused plaintiff's harm Not a defense when defendant:
  • is plaintiff's employer
  • is a hotel or common carrier
  • is a public servant/service
  • has substantially more bargaining power
Implied Plaintiff voluntarily accepted known risk of harm Not a defense when plaintiff:
  • suffered intentional harm
  • is member of statutorily protected class

A defendant is liable for negligence if he/she breaches a duty of care owed to the plaintiff and causes the plaintiff harm. However, assumption of the risk is a complete defense to negligence liability. Implied assumption of the risk arises when the plaintiff voluntarily engages in an activity with the knowledge that it carries inherent risks. For example, an athlete who participates in a sport implicitly assumes the inherent risks of that sport.*

Here, the linebacker may have breached the duty of care he owed to the quarterback by tackling him after the referee blew the whistle. However, this is the type of risk that is inherent to the sport of football, especially since the linebacker tackled the quarterback only two seconds after the whistle was blown. Therefore, the quarterback assumed the risk of being injured by a tackle while playing football, and he is unlikely to prevail in a negligence action (Choices C & D).

*Spectators similarly assume certain risks inherent in watching the sport (eg, the risk of being struck by a game ball).

(Choice A) Intent is irrelevant to negligence, which merely requires proof that the defendant's conduct fell below the applicable standard of care.

📌 Educational Objective

Implied assumption of the risk is a complete defense to negligence liability when the plaintiff voluntarily engages in an activity (eg, football) with the knowledge that it carries inherent risks (eg, risk of being injured during a tackle).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 496A-496C (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (assumption of risk principles).
questions.zh-question:
一名四分卫和一名后卫在一场职业橄榄球比赛中相互对抗。在比赛进行到某一时刻，该四分卫试图将橄榄球传给一名队友。与此同时，该后卫正在追赶该四分卫，以便在球被传出前擒抱他。就在后卫即将擒抱四分卫时，裁判吹响了哨子，示意本次进攻结束，球员们应停止当前行为。然而，后卫在哨声响起两秒后擒抱了四分卫，并导致四分卫手臂骨折。

如果四分卫对后卫提起过失诉讼，四分卫是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为后卫无意弄断四分卫的手臂。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为四分卫参加橄榄球比赛，即已自担其手臂骨折的风险。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为后卫违反了他对四分卫负有的注意义务。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为后卫在裁判吹哨后擒抱了四分卫。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence & Defenses
正确答案：选项 B 不会胜诉，因为四分卫参加橄榄球比赛，即已自担其手臂骨折的风险。
核心考点：默示风险自负
(Implied Assumption of Risk)

在侵权法中，如果原告自愿参与某项活动，且知晓该活动带有内在风险 (Inherent Risks)，则被告对该内在风险导致的伤害不承担过失责任。

1. 体育运动的特殊性：
职业橄榄球是一项剧烈的身体接触运动。参与者在踏上球场时，就被视为默示同意（Impliedly Consented）承受该运动中常见的身体接触和潜在伤害。

2. “内在风险”的范围：
虽然裁判吹响了哨子，但后卫在哨响后仅仅两秒就进行了擒抱。在激烈的比赛中，这种因惯性或反应时间导致的“迟来的撞击”被视为比赛的内在风险的一部分，而非超出比赛常规的异常行为。

3. 结论：
由于四分卫自愿参与比赛，他承担了被擒抱受伤的风险。风险自负是针对过失诉讼的完全抗辩 (Complete Defense)，因此四分卫无法胜诉。

为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 A (意图 Intent)： 错误。过失 (Negligence) 不需要证明被告有伤害的意图。即使后卫无意伤害，如果行为构成过失且无抗辩理由，仍需负责。但本题中抗辩理由成立。
  • 选项 C & D (注意义务 Duty of Care)： 错误。虽然在普通情境下，违反规则（哨响后撞人）可能构成违反注意义务，但在体育竞技的语境下，风险自负原则优先适用。只要行为没有达到“鲁莽 (Reckless)”或“故意不当行为 (Intentional Misconduct)”的程度，仅仅是比赛中的违规通常不足以支持过失索赔。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理体育竞技 (Sports Torts) 的题目时，请遵循以下逻辑：
1. 伤害是否源于运动的内在风险？如果是 ➡️ 风险自负 (Assumption of Risk)，被告无责。
2. 被告的行为是否极其恶劣（如斗殴、明显超出比赛范围的暴力）？如果是 ➡️ 可能构成鲁莽 (Recklessness) 或 殴打 (Battery)，被告需负责。

关键点：仅仅违反比赛规则（如犯规）通常不足以推翻风险自负的抗辩。

reason.en: Football participation triggers implied assumption of inherent contact injuries.
reason.zh: 参与橄榄球运动可触发对固有接触伤风险的默示接受。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A driver, returning home from a long work shift at a factory, fell asleep at the wheel and lost control of his car. As a result, his car collided with a police car driven by an officer who was returning to the station after having responded to an emergency. The officer was injured in the accident and later sued the driver in negligence for her injuries. The driver has moved for summary judgment, arguing that the common law firefighter's rule bars the suit.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because the firefighter's rule does not apply to police officers.
choices.B: No, because the police officer's injuries were not related to any special dangers of her job.
choices.C: Yes, because the accident would not have occurred but for the emergency.
choices.D: Yes, because the police officer was injured on the job.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Rescue doctrine
General rule Rescuers can recover for injuries sustained while attempting to rescue another if that person's peril was caused by defendant's negligence
Exception
(firefighter's rule)		 Professional rescuers cannot recover for injuries attributable to special dangers of their job—eg:
  • firefighter entering burning building
  • police officer arresting suspect
  • paramedic/lifeguard attempting risky rescue

When a person's conduct creates a risk of harm, he/she owes a duty to all foreseeable plaintiffs. Under the rescue doctrine, foreseeable plaintiffs include rescuers who might be harmed while attempting to aid victims of the risky conduct. But the rescue doctrine is limited by the common law firefighter's rule, which applies to all professional rescuers (eg, police officers) (Choice A). This rule bars recovery in negligence if the professional rescuer's harm resulted from a special danger of his/her job.

Here, the officer was injured in a car accident and later sued the driver in negligence for her injuries. The officer's injuries were not related to any special dangers of her job since the risk of being struck by a car in normal traffic applies to everyone on the road. Therefore, the firefighter's rule does not bar the officer's recovery, and the court should deny the driver's motion for summary judgment.

(Choice C) The emergency—from which the officer was returning—was an actual cause of the accident since it would not have occurred but for the emergency. But this does not justify summary judgment for the driver since his conduct (ie, falling asleep at the wheel) was also an actual cause of the accident.

(Choice D) Although the police officer was injured on the job, her injury did not result from any special danger of police work. Therefore, summary judgment for the driver would be improper.

📌 Educational Objective

The firefighter's rule is a limitation on the rescue doctrine that bars firefighters and other professional rescuers from recovering in negligence for harm that resulted from the special dangers of their jobs. But they can still recover for injuries that arose from risks applicable to everyone.

📚 References
  • 62 Am. Jur. 2d Premises Liability § 421 (2019) (explaining that the firefighter's rule prevents professional rescuers from recovering for injuries arising out of the special risks of their professions).
  • Vasquez v. N. Cty. Transit Dist., 292 F.3d 1049, 1054–55 (9th Cir. 2002) (explaining that the firefighter's rule extends to police officers).

一名司机在工厂上完长班开车回家途中，在驾驶时睡着并导致车辆失控。结果，他的车撞上了一辆警车，该警车由一名处理完紧急情况后返回警局的警官驾驶。该警官在事故中受伤，后以过失为由起诉该司机，要求赔偿其所受伤害。该司机已提出即决判决动议，主张普通法上的“消防员规则”（firefighter's rule）禁止该诉讼。

法院是否应批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为“消防员规则”不适用于警官。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该警官的受伤与她工作的任何特殊危险无关。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为若无该紧急情况，则事故不会发生。
zh-choices.D: 应该，因为该警官是在执行公务时受伤的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 过失 (Negligence)
正确答案
选项 B
不应批准，因为该警官的受伤与她工作的任何特殊危险无关。
⚖️ 核心法律原则：消防员规则
The Firefighter's Rule (消防员规则)

这是一个普通法上的规则，通常作为被告的抗辩理由。它规定：

  • 原则：专业救援人员（如警察、消防员）不能因其工作所针对的固有风险 (Inherent Risks) 而起诉造成该风险的人。
  • 理由：他们已经因承担这些风险而获得了薪酬（包括工资和伤残福利），且公众不应因寻求帮助而面临被起诉的风险。
🔍 案件深度解析

为什么本案中不能使用消防员规则作为抗辩？

1. 区分“固有风险”与“一般风险”：
消防员规则只禁止对工作特有危险（Special Dangers/Inherent Risks）的索赔。例如：

  • 消防员在救火时被烧伤。
  • 警察在逮捕嫌疑人时被袭击。
  • 警察在高速追捕嫌疑人时发生车祸。

2. 本案事实应用：
在本案中，警官是在处理完紧急情况后返回警局的途中被撞的。肇事司机是因为疲劳驾驶（与警官的职责无关）撞上了警车。

关键点：这种车祸风险（被其他疲劳驾驶的司机撞击）是道路上每个人都面临的普通风险，并不是警察工作所特有的“特殊危险”。

因此，该规则不适用，警官可以像普通公民一样起诉司机的过失。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A 错误：
虽然结论（不批准）是对的，但理由错误。消防员规则（Firefighter's Rule）在普通法下确实适用于警察和其他专业救援人员，不仅仅是消防员。
选项 C 错误：
这是关于事实因果关系 (Actual Cause) 的论述。虽然“若无紧急情况警官不会在那”，但这并不是禁止索赔的法律理由。被告不能因为原告恰好在场就免除责任。
选项 D 错误：
仅仅“在执行公务期间 (on the job)”受伤并不足以触发消防员规则。必须是该工作特有的风险导致了伤害。如果是普通风险（如本案），即使在工作时间，也可以索赔。

遇到涉及 Firefighter's Rule 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 原告是否为专业救援人员？（是）
  2. 伤害是否由其工作意图处理的特定风险（如火灾、正在追捕的罪犯）造成的？
  3. 如果是独立的过失（如第三方撞击、房主未告知的隐藏陷阱、或与救援任务无关的普通风险），则该规则不适用，原告可以索赔。

A.text: does not apply to police officers
