questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A young woman who attended a rock concert at a nightclub was injured when the band opened its performance with illegal fireworks that ignited foam insulation in the club's ceiling and walls. The young woman sued the radio station that sponsored the performance. The radio station has moved for summary judgment, claiming that it owed no duty to audience members.
The evidence has established the following facts: The station advertised its sponsorship on the radio and in print, distributed free tickets to the concert, staffed the event with the station's interns to assist with crowd control, and provided a station disc jockey to serve as master of ceremonies. The master of ceremonies had the authority to stop or delay the performance at any time on the basis of any safety concern. The station knew or should have known that the band routinely used unlicensed, illegal fireworks in its performances.
Should the court grant the radio station's motion for summary judgment?

choices.A: No, because there is sufficient evidence of knowledge and control on the part of the station to impose on it a duty of care to audience members.
choices.B: No, because under respondeat superior, the radio station is vicariously liable for the negligent actions of the band.
choices.C: Yes, because it is the band and the nightclub owners who owed audience members a duty of care.
choices.D: Yes, because the conduct of the band in setting off illegal fireworks was criminal and was a superseding cause as a matter of law.

questions.explanation:
Defendant's motion for summary judgment
For negligence,
Plaintiff must provide sufficient evidence that
defendant owed plaintiff a duty to use reasonable care
Yes
NoGrant motion
defendant breached that duty
Yes
NoGrant motion
defendant caused plaintiff harm
Yes
NoGrant motion
Deny motion

A defendant's motion for summary judgment should be granted where there is insufficient evidence to support one or more elements of the plaintiff's claim. Therefore, summary judgment for the defendant is warranted on a negligence claim when there is no evidence that the:

• owed the plaintiff a duty to use reasonable care
• breached that duty or
• caused the plaintiff harm.

When the defendant is a land possessor (ie, one who occupies and controls the land), the defendant owes a duty to use reasonable care to identify and mitigate any foreseeable risk of harm to land entrants.

Here, the radio station was a land possessor as it staffed the event (occupation) and provided a disc jockey who had the authority to stop the concert for any safety concern (control). And since the station knew or should have known that the band routinely used illegal fireworks in its performances, the risk of a fire was foreseeable. Therefore, there is sufficient evidence that the station owed audience members a duty to use reasonable care to identify and mitigate that risk, so the station's motion for summary judgment should be denied.

(Choice B) The doctrine of respondeat superior holds employers vicariously liable for their employees' torts. Here, the band was not the radio station's employee, so this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice C) Although the band and nightclub owners likely owed the audience a duty of care, that does not eliminate the radio station's concurrent duty of care.

(Choice D) Here, the band's illegal use of fireworks was reasonably foreseeable, so its conduct was not a superseding cause and does not absolve the station of liability.

📌 Educational Objective

Land possessors—persons who occupy and control the land—owe land entrants a duty to use reasonable care to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks of harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm §§ 49, 51 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (duty owed by land possessors).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a) (motion for summary judgment).
questions.zh-question:
一名年轻女子在一家夜总会参加摇滚音乐会时，因乐队用非法烟花作为表演开场，点燃了俱乐部天花板和墙壁的泡沫隔音材料而受伤。该女子起诉了赞助该表演的广播电台。广播电台已申请即决判决，声称其对观众不负有任何义务。

证据已证实以下事实：该电台通过广播和印刷品宣传其赞助，分发了音乐会的免费门票，安排电台实习生在活动现场协助人群控制，并提供一名电台唱片骑师担任司仪。该司仪有权出于任何安全顾虑随时停止或推迟表演。该电台知道或应该知道该乐队在其表演中常规性地使用未经许可的非法烟花。

法院是否应批准广播电台的即决判决动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为有充分证据表明电台方面知情并行使控制，足以使其对观众成员承担注意义务。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为根据“雇主责任”原则 (respondeat superior)，广播电台对乐队的过失行为负有转承责任。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为对观众成员负有注意义务的是乐队和夜总会所有者。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为乐队燃放非法烟花的行为属于刑事犯罪，并且在法律上构成一项替代性原因。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts (侵权法) - Negligence
正确答案：A 不应批准即决判决。
因为有充分证据表明电台具有知情权和控制权，从而对观众负有注意义务。
⚖️ 核心法律依据
🏗️ 土地占有者的义务 (Duty of Land Possessors)

在侵权法中，注意义务不仅仅源于所有权 (Ownership)，更源于占有和控制 (Possession and Control)。

即使广播电台不拥有夜总会，但它通过以下行为成为了事实上的“土地占有者”：

  • 占用 (Occupation)： 派遣实习生进行人群控制。
  • 控制 (Control)： 提供的司仪 (MC) 有权因安全问题随时叫停演出。
🔍 即决判决的标准 (Summary Judgment Standard)

被告申请即决判决通常基于“没有注意义务” (No Duty)。

如果原告能证明被告对现场有控制权且风险是可预见的 (Foreseeable)，那么被告就负有识别和减轻风险的义务。因此，法院不能认定被告“无义务”，必须驳回即决判决动议。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 B (Respondeat Superior)

错误点：雇主替代责任 (Vicarious Liability) 仅适用于雇佣关系。乐队通常是独立合同工 (Independent Contractors)，而非电台雇员，因此电台不对乐队的过失承担替代责任。电台的责任源于其自身的过失（未能行使控制权防止已知危险）。

选项 C (Concurrent Duty)

错误点：虽然乐队和夜总会确实有义务，但这并不具有排他性。侵权法中存在共同义务 (Concurrent Duty)。电台不能因为别人也有责任就推卸自己因“控制现场”而产生的责任。

选项 D (Superseding Cause)

错误点：这是一个常见的陷阱。通常犯罪行为会切断因果链，但如果该犯罪行为是可预见的 (Foreseeable)，则不会切断。题目明确指出电台“知道或应该知道”乐队使用非法烟花，因此这是可预见的风险，不构成替代性原因。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Negligence (过失) 题目时，如果被告申请 Summary Judgment 声称 "No Duty"：

  1. 寻找被告是否对环境或第三方行使了控制 (Control)。
  2. 寻找风险是否可预见 (Foreseeable)。

如果两者皆有，法院通常会认定存在 Duty，从而驳回被告的动议。

MBE Torts Question Analysis | Q83828

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A plumbing company hired a worker to work at various construction sites. The worker used his own truck to travel between the company's warehouse and the construction sites, but the company fitted the truck with a rack for carrying plumbing pipes. The company paid the worker for traveling between the warehouse and the construction sites, but not for his drive to and from work.
Because the worker was required to haul pipes on his truck while driving between the warehouse and the construction sites, the company asked the worker, before hiring him, whether he had a valid driver's license. The worker represented that he did, although in fact his license had been suspended because he had been convicted of recklessly causing motor vehicle collisions. The company made no effort to verify the worker's representation.
While driving to work one morning in his truck, the worker carelessly caused a collision in which a woman was injured.
In her subsequent action against the plumbing company, based on a theory of negligent hiring, is the woman likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the actions taken by the worker were not in the performance of his employment or job duties.
choices.B: No, because the worker was an independent contractor.
choices.C: Yes, because the company fitted the worker's truck with a pipe rack.
choices.D: Yes, because the company had a duty to ensure that its workers had valid driver's licenses.

questions.explanation:
Drive to work
(off the clock)
Accident occurs
≠

& construction sites

Liability for negligent hiring arises when a defendant's failure to use reasonable care in hiring a competent worker causes the plaintiff harm. Therefore, a defendant is only liable for negligent hiring if there is a causal connection between the defendant's negligence in hiring the worker, the worker's employment or job duties, and the plaintiff's harm.

Here, the plumbing company failed to use reasonable care when it made no effort to verify that the worker—who was paid to drive between the warehouse and various construction sites—had a valid driver's license ((Choice D)). But even though the worker carelessly collided with the woman, it occurred during his commute to work—not during his employment or performance of job duties (no causal connection). Therefore, the plumbing company is not liable for negligent hiring.

(Choice B) A defendant can be liable for negligent hiring of an employee or an independent contractor. Therefore, the fact that the worker was an independent contractor will not defeat the woman's claim. Instead, her claim will fail because the worker was not acting in performance of his employment or job duties when the collision occurred.

(Choice C) Although the plumbing company fitted the worker's truck with a pipe rack, it only paid him to drive the truck between the warehouse and construction sites—not to and from work. And since the collision occurred while he was driving to work (not while performing job duties), the company is not liable for the woman's injury.

📌 Educational Objective

Liability for negligent hiring arises when a defendant's failure to use reasonable care in hiring a competent worker causes the plaintiff harm—ie, there must be some causal connection between the defendant's negligence in hiring the worker, the worker's employment or job duties, and the plaintiff's harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency § 7.05 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (negligent hiring).
Torts · Negligence · Vicarious liability

一家管道公司雇佣了一名工人在多个建筑工地工作。该工人使用自己的卡车在公司仓库和建筑工地之间往返，但公司为该卡车安装了一个用于承载管道的架子。公司支付工人在仓库和建筑工地之间往返的报酬，但不支付其上下班的通勤费用。

由于该工人在仓库和建筑工地之间驾驶时需要用其卡车运输管道，公司在雇佣他之前询问他是否持有有效驾照。该工人声称他有驾照，但实际上他的驾照因曾被判鲁莽驾驶导致机动车碰撞而被吊销。公司未曾试图核实该工人的陈述。

一天早上，该工人在驾车上班途中，因疏忽造成了一起碰撞事故，导致一名女性受伤。

在该女性随后以雇佣过失理论对管道公司提起的诉讼中，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该工人的行为并非在履行其雇佣或工作职责。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该工人是一名独立承包人。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为公司为该工人的卡车安装了管道架。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为公司有责任确保其工人持有有效驾照。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligent Hiring & Scope of Employment
侵权法 (Torts)
核心法律原则：雇佣过失 (Negligent Hiring)

雇主若在雇佣员工时未尽到合理注意义务（例如未核查背景），且该过失是导致原告受伤的近因 (Proximate Cause)，则雇主需承担责任。

关键点：雇主的过失必须与员工的工作职责 (Job Duties) 以及原告的伤害之间存在因果联系。
案情关键点分析
  • 过失存在：公司未核实驾照，雇佣了有鲁莽驾驶前科的工人。
  • 工作范围：公司支付工地间的交通费，但不支付上下班通勤费。
  • 事故发生时机：工人在上班途中 (Commuting) 发生事故。
深度解析

本题考察的是因果关系 (Causation) 的界限。

虽然公司在雇佣过程中存在过失（未检查驾照），但要让公司承担责任，原告必须证明这种“雇佣过失”是导致伤害的法律原因。

根据普通法原则，通勤规则 (Going and Coming Rule) 通常认定员工在上下班途中的行为不属于受雇范围。此时，工人驾驶的是自己的卡车，处于私人时间。虽然卡车上装有公司的架子，但这并没有改变他在“通勤”这一事实。

由于事故发生在工人履行工作职责之外的时间，公司“未能检查驾照”的过失与“通勤期间的事故”之间缺乏必要的法律因果联系。换句话说，公司雇佣他去工地干活，并没有“导致”他在上班路上的私人驾驶行为造成事故。

正确答案：A

不会胜诉，因为该工人的行为并非在履行其雇佣或工作职责。

理由： 责任链条在“工作职责”处断裂。如果事故发生在从仓库去工地的路上，公司很可能因为 Negligent Hiring 负责；但因为是在通勤路上，公司不负责。

干扰项排除
选项 B (独立承包人)： 错误。雇佣过失 (Negligent Hiring) 理论既适用于雇员 (Employee) 也适用于独立承包人 (Independent Contractor)。如果是替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)，身份区分才至关重要。
选项 C (管道架)： 错误。虽然安装了架子，但这只是为了工作的便利，并没有将工人的私人通勤时间转化为工作时间。
选项 D (公司有责任)： 这是一个典型的“正确陈述但结论错误”的选项。公司确实有责任 (Duty) 确保工人有驾照，但原告败诉的原因不是因为公司没责任，而是因为公司的违约行为不是导致此次特定伤害的法律原因 (Lack of Proximate Cause)。
MBE 解题技巧：
在处理雇主责任题目时，首先区分是 Respondeat Superior (替代责任) 还是 Negligent Hiring (自身过失)。但无论哪种理论，都要仔细检查事故是否发生在与工作相关的活动中。通勤 (Commuting) 通常是雇主的免责金牌。

reason.zh: 该索赔既要求雇用过失，也要求损害发生在职务相关活动中。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An employer retained a doctor to conduct physical examinations of prospective employees. After reviewing one applicant's test results, the doctor informed the employer and the applicant that the applicant suffered from AIDS. The applicant was shocked by this news and suffered a heart attack as a result. One month later, the applicant learned that she in fact did not have AIDS and that the doctor had negligently confused her file with that of another prospective employee.
If the applicant sues the doctor to recover damages, under which cause(s) of action is she most likely to prevail?

choices.A: Invasion of privacy.
choices.B: Invasion of privacy and negligent misrepresentation.
choices.C: Negligent infliction of emotional distress.
choices.D: Negligent infliction of emotional distress and negligent misrepresentation.

questions.explanation:
Negligent infliction of emotional distress
Theories of recoveryRequired elements
Zone of danger
  • Defendant's negligence put plaintiff in danger of immediate bodily harm
  • Danger caused plaintiff serious emotional distress
Bystander
  • Defendant negligently injured plaintiff's close relative
  • Plaintiff contemporaneously perceived that event
  • Event caused plaintiff serious emotional distress
Special situations
  • Defendant negligently:
    • delivered erroneous announcement of death or illness
    • mishandled corpse or bodily remains
    • contaminated food with repulsive foreign object
  • Caused plaintiff serious emotional distress

A plaintiff can recover for negligent infliction of emotional distress (NIED) in three situations: (1) zone of danger, (2) bystander, or (3) special situations. Liability under the special-situations theory arises when the plaintiff suffers serious emotional distress because the defendant negligently:

  • delivered an erroneous announcement of death or illness
  • mishandled a corpse or bodily remains or
  • contaminated food with a repulsive foreign object.

Here, the doctor negligently misdiagnosed the applicant with AIDS because he confused her file with that of another prospective employee. The erroneous announcement of this illness caused the applicant serious emotional distress—she went into shock and suffered a heart attack upon being informed of this diagnosis. As a result, she will most likely prevail on her cause of action against the doctor for NIED.

(Choices A & B) There are four theories of recovery for invasion of privacy—none of which apply here. That is because the doctor did not (1) conduct the physical examination of the applicant without her authorization (ie, no intrusion upon seclusion), (2) publicize her private information, (3) publicize the misdiagnosis to cast her in a false light, or (4) use her name or likeness for personal benefit.

(Choices B & D) Negligent misrepresentation occurs in a commercial setting when (1) the defendant negligently provides the plaintiff with false information and (2) the plaintiff reasonably relies on that information and suffers pecuniary loss. Here, the doctor provided the applicant with false information, but she never relied on his misdiagnosis. Therefore, negligent misrepresentation does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Negligent infliction of emotional distress occurs under the special-situations theory when the plaintiff suffers serious emotional distress because the defendant negligently: (1) delivered an erroneous announcement of death or illness, (2) mishandled a corpse or bodily remains, or (3) contaminated food with a repulsive foreign object.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 47(b) cmt. f (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (special-situations theory of negligent infliction of emotional distress).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 652A–652E (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (invasion of privacy).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 552 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (negligent misrepresentation).
questions.zh-question:
一名雇主委托一名医生对未来的雇员进行体检。在审查一名申请人的检测结果后，该医生告知雇主和该申请人，该申请人患有艾滋病。申请人对这一消息感到震惊，并因此心脏病发作。一个月后，该申请人得知她实际上并未患有艾滋病，而医生因过失混淆了她与另一位未来雇员的档案。

如果该申请人起诉医生以获得损害赔偿，她最有可能根据哪项诉因获胜？

zh-choices.A: 侵犯隐私权。
zh-choices.B: 侵犯隐私权与过失性失实陈述。
zh-choices.C: 过失导致的精神痛苦。
zh-choices.D: 过失导致的精神痛苦与过失性失实陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
Torts / Negligence

核心考点：过失导致的精神痛苦

Negligent Infliction of Emotional Distress (NIED)

本题考察的是侵权法中一个非常具体但经典的规则：在特定情况下，因错误通知疾病导致的严重精神痛苦。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

通常情况下，原告要主张 NIED，必须证明自己处于“危险区域” (Zone of Danger) 或符合“旁观者” (Bystander) 规则。

但在 MBE 考试中，还有第三类“特殊情况” (Special Situations)，被告因其过失行为极易引发严重精神痛苦，即使没有身体撞击，也需承担责任。主要包括：

  • 传递错误的死亡或疾病通知 (Erroneous report of death or illness)
  • 不当处理尸体 (Mishandling of a corpse)

✅ 为什么选 C？

过失导致的精神痛苦 (NIED)

在本案中，医生与申请人之间存在医患关系（或类似的专业关系），医生负有谨慎义务。

  1. 过失行为：医生混淆了档案，错误地告知申请人她患有艾滋病（一种严重的致命疾病）。
  2. 后果：这一消息直接导致申请人极度震惊并心脏病发作（严重的精神痛苦及身体伤害）。

这完全符合 NIED 中的“特殊情况”理论。法院认为，错误地告知某人患有绝症，自然且可预见地会导致其遭受严重的精神打击。因此，申请人无需证明她在物理上处于被撞击的“危险区域”，即可胜诉。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

A & B: 侵犯隐私权 (Invasion of Privacy)

侵犯隐私权通常包含四种类型，但本案均不符合：

  • 公开私密事实/虚假形象：医生只告诉了雇主和申请人本人，没有向公众“公开” (Publicity)。
  • 侵扰安宁：体检是经过授权的。

关键点：没有向大众传播，就不构成隐私侵权中的公开类诉因。

B & D: 过失性失实陈述 (Negligent Misrepresentation)

这个诉因通常用于商业或经济损失的场景。

  • 要素：被告在商业交易中提供虚假信息，原告信赖该信息并遭受金钱损失 (Pecuniary Loss)。
  • 本案：申请人遭受的是身体伤害和精神痛苦（心脏病），而不是因为信赖错误信息去做了某笔亏本生意。

💡

区分损害类型是关键：

  • 如果是身体伤害/精神痛苦 ➡️ 优先考虑 Negligence / NIED。
  • 如果是名誉受损 ➡️ 考虑 Defamation / False Light。
  • 如果是金钱/商业损失 ➡️ 考虑 Misrepresentation。

看到“错误的绝症诊断”导致“休克/心脏病”，直接定位到 NIED 的特殊情况例外。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pedestrian was walking on a crowded public path when she was struck by a speeding bicyclist who swerved wildly to avoid a jogger. As a result, the pedestrian suffered a dislocated vertebra in her spine that would have required several months of treatment to completely heal. The jogger, who witnessed the accident, had no medical training but believed in good faith that it was medically necessary to lift the pedestrian's head and slip his jacket underneath. This unnecessary act resulted in additional damage to the pedestrian's spine that left the pedestrian permanently unable to walk.
This jurisdiction has enacted the following Good Samaritan statute: "Any person who in good faith renders gratuitous emergency medical care or assistance shall not be liable for civil damages for any act or omission, not amounting to gross negligence, in rendering such aid."
In a suit against both the bicyclist and the jogger for negligence, is the pedestrian likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the jogger's act is protected by the statute and is a superseding cause that cut off the bicyclist's liability.
choices.B: Yes, but only against the bicyclist because the jogger's conduct was a foreseeable intervening cause.
choices.C: Yes, but only against the jogger because his gross negligence actually caused the pedestrian's enhanced injury.
choices.D: Yes, since both the bicyclist and the jogger are jointly and severally liable for the pedestrian's injury.

questions.explanation:
Standards of care for negligence
AdultMust act in same manner as ordinary, reasonable adult in similar circumstances
• Standard adjusted for physical disabilities, superior skill & knowledge, involuntary intoxication
• Standard not adjusted for mental & emotional disabilities, voluntary intoxication
ProfessionalMust demonstrate same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
• National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
ChildMust act in same manner as reasonable child of same age, intelligence & experience
• Adult standard applied to children engaged in dangerous adult activity
• Children under five years old incapable of negligence

*A modern trend applies a national standard of care to all physicians.

A plaintiff will prevail on a negligence claim if four elements are established: duty, breach, causation, and damages. Duty refers to the obligation to protect another against unreasonable risk of injury. The duty of care is imposed on a defendant is that of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances—ie, one in the defendant's same position, with the same information and level of competence.

Here, the bicyclist breached the duty of care by speeding and swerving wildly to avoid a jogger since a reasonably prudent person would ride in a controlled manner. Since that breach caused the bicyclist to hit and injure the pedestrian, the bicyclist is liable for negligence.

The jogger's attempted aid did not negate the bicyclist's liability because it was not a superseding cause—ie, an unforeseeable intervening event that breaks the chain of proximate causation between the defendant's tortious act and the plaintiff's harm. Instead, the jogger's intervention was foreseeable and occurred after the plaintiff's injury (Choice A).

This foreseeable intervention would make the jogger jointly and severally liable to the plaintiff if his actions were negligent. But less may be expected of a reasonably prudent person forced to act in an emergency such as this one—so long as the defendant's conduct did not cause the emergency.*

Here, the jogger acted as a reasonably prudent person during the emergency by rendering aid to the injured pedestrian. Therefore, the jogger did not breach a duty of care—and is not liable for negligence—even though his aid exacerbated the pedestrian's injuries. Even if the jogger had been negligent, he would have been shielded by the jurisdiction's Good Samaritan statute since his actions did not amount to gross negligence. As a result, the pedestrian will not prevail against the jogger (Choice B) & (C) & (D).

*But if the defendant's conduct created the emergency, then the defendant may be liable for failing to rescue the plaintiff from that situation even if a reasonably prudent person would not have been expected to do so.

📌 Educational Objective

The duty of care imposed on a defendant is that of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances—ie, one in the defendant's same position, with the same information and level of competence. Therefore, less may be expected of a reasonably prudent person acting in an emergency.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 283 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (reasonable-man standard).
questions.zh-question:
一名行人在拥挤的公共小径上行走时，被一名为躲避慢跑者而猛烈转向的超速自行车手撞倒。结果，该行人的脊椎发生一节椎骨脱臼，需要数月治疗才能完全康复。目睹了这起事故的慢跑者没有受过任何医学训练，但他真诚地认为，在医疗上有必要抬起行人的头部，并将自己的夹克垫在下面。这一不必要的行为对行人的脊椎造成了额外的损害，导致该行人永久无法行走。

该司法管辖区颁布了以下《好撒玛利亚人法》(Good Samaritan statute)：“任何真诚地提供无偿紧急医疗护理或援助的人，在提供此类援助的过程中，对其任何作为或不作为，只要不构成重大过失，均不承担民事损害赔偿责任。”

在一场针对自行车手和慢跑者的过失诉讼中，行人是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为慢跑者的行为受到法规保护，并且是一个切断了自行车手责任的替代性原因（superseding cause）。
zh-choices.B: 会，但只能针对自行车手胜诉，因为慢跑者的行为是一个可预见的介入原因（intervening cause）。
zh-choices.C: 会，但只能针对慢跑者胜诉，因为他的重大过失（gross negligence）实际造成了行人伤势的加重。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为自行车手和慢跑者均需对行人的伤害承担连带责任（jointly and severally liable）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Negligence & Intervening Causes
📚 核心考点 (Key Concepts)

本题考察两个关键的侵权法原则：

  1. 介入原因 (Intervening Cause) 与原告的责任范围。
  2. 好撒玛利亚人法 (Good Samaritan Statutes) 对救援者的保护。
1 自行车手的责任 (Bicyclist's Liability)

自行车手超速并猛烈转向，这明显违反了注意义务 (Duty of Care)，构成了过失。

关键在于：他是否要对慢跑者造成的二次伤害负责？

根据侵权法原则，"Danger invites rescue" (危险招致救援)。如果被告的过失造成了危险局面，那么第三方（如慢跑者或医生）介入救援是可预见的 (Foreseeable)。

因此，救援者的普通过失（Ordinary Negligence）属于可预见的介入原因 (Foreseeable Intervening Cause)，它不会切断原始致害人（自行车手）的因果关系链。自行车手需对全部伤害（包括二次伤害）负责。

2 慢跑者的责任 (Jogger's Liability)

慢跑者虽然造成了额外伤害，但他是在紧急情况下真诚地提供无偿援助。

题目明确指出该地有《好撒玛利亚人法》 (Good Samaritan Statute)。这类法规通常规定，除非救援者的行为构成重大过失 (Gross Negligence) 或故意不当行为，否则免除其民事责任。

判定：慢跑者虽然缺乏医学常识（移动了伤者头部），但他出于善意且无受训背景，这种错误属于一般过失，很难被认定为“重大过失”（即极度漠视他人安全的鲁莽行为）。因此，法规保护他免受起诉。

选项深度解析
正确 选项 B

行人胜诉，但仅针对自行车手。

自行车手不仅要对第一次撞击负责，还要对慢跑者造成的二次伤害负责，因为救援行为是其过失行为的可预见后果。同时，慢跑者因法规保护而免责。

错误 选项 A

错误在于认为慢跑者的行为是 Superseding Cause (替代性原因)。只有不可预见 (Unforeseeable) 的事件（如天灾或第三方的故意犯罪）才会切断因果链。救援中的失误通常被视为可预见的。

错误 选项 C

错误在于认定慢跑者存在 Gross Negligence (重大过失)。题目描述他"believed in good faith"（真诚相信）且无医学背景，这不足以构成重大过失，因此他受法规保护。

错误 选项 D

既然慢跑者不承担责任（Not Liable），就不存在与自行车手承担 Joint and Several Liability (连带责任) 的基础。

💡 MBE 提分技巧
在处理涉及“二次伤害”的题目时，记住这个公式：
原始致害人责任 = 初始伤害 + 救援/医疗造成的加重伤害

除非救援行为极其离谱（如医生故意伤害病人），否则原始致害人很难甩锅。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The owner of an apple orchard rented space in the loft of a local farmer's barn to store her harvested apples each year until they were frozen and ready to be pressed for ice cider in the spring. Each fall, the orchard owner hired workers to harvest the apples, store them in barrels, and transport the barrels to the farmer's loft. The farmer also rents space in the loft to other farmers, who can rearrange the loft's contents to make room to store their crops. One winter, the farmer was working in his barn when a barrel of frozen apples rolled off the loft and struck him, causing severe injuries. The farmer has sued the orchard owner for negligence and established all of these facts at trial before resting his case. The farmer has also established that the barrel would not have rolled off the loft unless it had been negligently placed on its side.
Can the orchard owner succeed in a motion for a directed verdict?

choices.A: No, because an employer may be vicariously liable for her employee's torts.
choices.B: No, because the barrel would not have injured the farmer in the absence of negligence.
choices.C: Yes, because the jury may not properly infer negligent conduct by either the orchard owner or her employees.
choices.D: Yes, because the orchard owner cannot be held liable for any injury that occurred on the farmer's property.

questions.explanation:
Proving negligence

Res ipsa loquitur

Inferred if:
  • Accident of kind that usually does not occur in absence of negligence
  • Δ in exclusive control of thing that caused harm
  • TT did not cause harm
Δ owed TT duty of care
↓
Δ breached duty

Negligence per se

Established if:
  • Law imposes duty on Δ
  • Δ violated law
  • TT was in class of persons law intended to protect
  • TT suffered type of harm law intended to prevent
Breach actually & proximately caused TT physical harm
TT's damages traceable to physical harm
Liable for negligence
Δ = defendant; TT = plaintiff.

In the absence of direct evidence of negligence (as seen here), the traditional doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows the defendant's negligence to be inferred when the plaintiff shows that the accident was:

• of a kind that ordinarily does not occur in the absence of negligence
• caused by an agent or instrumentality within the exclusive control of the defendant and
• not due to any action on the part of the plaintiff.

If the plaintiff fails to provide sufficient evidence to support an inference of negligence (i.e., no reasonable jury could find in the plaintiff's favor), the court should grant the defendant's motion for a directed verdict.

Here, the farmer sued the orchard owner after being injured by a barrel of frozen apples that rolled off the loft leased to the owner. The farmer established that the barrel would not have rolled off the loft unless it had been negligently placed on its side. But several other farmers stored their crops in the loft as well, and the farmer presented no evidence that would tend to eliminate the other farmers as potential causes. On these facts, the jury may not properly infer negligent conduct by the owner or her employees. Therefore, the owner can succeed in a motion for a directed verdict.

(Choice A) An employer can be held vicariously liable for her employees' acts under the doctrine of respondeat superior. However, the plaintiff must first demonstrate negligence by the employee (not seen here).

(Choice B) The barrel would not have injured the farmer in the absence of negligence. But here, the farmer failed to provide evidence tending to eliminate the other farmers as the cause of his injuries.

(Choice D) As a tenant (possessor of land), the owner could be liable for injuries that occurred on the farmer's property if she created a dangerous condition on the property that caused injury. But here, the farmer presented no evidence demonstrating that the owner created such a dangerous condition.

📌 Educational Objective

The traditional doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows the defendant's negligence to be inferred when the plaintiff shows that the accident was (1) of a kind that ordinarily does not occur in the absence of negligence, (2) caused by an agent or instrumentality within the exclusive control of the defendant, and (3) not due to any action on the part of the plaintiff.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 328D (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining when a defendant's negligence can be inferred based on the type of accident that injured the plaintiff).

主题：侵权法（Torts）— 过失（Negligence）

题目：
一位苹果园主每年都会在当地一位农民谷仓的阁楼里租用一块空间，用来存放她收获的苹果，直到这些苹果被冻住，并在春天被压榨制成冰苹果酒（ice cider）。每年秋天，果园主都会雇人采摘苹果、把苹果装入木桶，然后将木桶运到这位农民的阁楼里。该农民还把阁楼空间出租给其他农民，这些农民可以重新摆放阁楼里的物品，以腾出空间存放自己的农作物。某个冬天，这位农民正在谷仓里工作时，一只装着冻结苹果的木桶从阁楼上滚落下来，砸中了他，造成严重伤害。农民以过失（negligence）为由起诉果园主，并在举证完毕后，于审判中证明了以上所有事实。农民还证明，该木桶若不是被疏忽地侧放，就不会从阁楼上滚落下来。
果园主能否在请求指令性裁决（motion for a directed verdict）中胜诉？

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An adult gave a pack of cigarettes to a minor whom the adult incorrectly believed to be an adult. The minor took the cigarettes to a nearby property where he climbed on top of a stack of fence posts, lit a cigarette, and began smoking it. Shortly thereafter, the minor unintentionally dropped the lit cigarette into the stack of fence posts. The minor tried to retrieve the cigarette so that he could extinguish it, but he was unable to do so. Then the minor wandered away. The lit cigarette subsequently set fire to the fence posts, resulting in the destruction of the posts as well as an adjacent garage and its contents.
The jurisdiction has a strict liability statute that makes it a misdemeanor to provide a minor with cigarettes. Violation of the statute is punishable by a $200 fine.
The owner of the destroyed property initiated a negligence lawsuit against the adult.
Which of the following is the adult's WEAKEST defense to this action?

choices.A: The adult did not know that the minor was underage when he gave the cigarettes to him.
choices.B: The destruction of the property is not a type of harm against which the statute was intended to protect.
choices.C: The destruction of the property was not proximately caused by the adult's violation of the statute.
choices.D: The property owner is not in the class of people intended to be protected by the statute.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Negligence liability
Δ owed TT duty of care
↓
Δ breached duty
↓
Breach actually & proximately caused TT physical harm
↓
TT's damages traceable to physical harm
↓
Liable for negligence
Δ = defendant; TT = plaintiff.
Negligence per se
Presumed if:
• Δ violated statute
• TT suffered type of harm statute was intended to prevent
• TT was in class of persons statute was intended to protect

Negligence requires proof of the following elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. Duty and breach are presumed under the doctrine of negligence per se when the following facts are proved:

  • The defendant violated a statute or ordinance.
  • The plaintiff suffered a type of harm that the statute or ordinance was intended to protect against.
  • The plaintiff was in the class of persons intended to be protected by the statute or ordinance.

Here, the jurisdiction's statute makes it a strict liability offense to provide a minor with cigarettes. This means that liability can be imposed without proof of fault. Therefore, the fact that the adult did not know that the minor was underage when he gave the cigarettes to him is no defense to the adult's violation of the statute—or to this negligence per se action.

However, the adult may be able to successfully defend this action on one or more of the following grounds:

(Choice B) The harm that the statute was intended to protect against is harm to minors from smoking—not property destruction caused by cigarettes (Choice B).

(Choice D) The class of persons that the statute was intended to protect is minors—not property owners who suffer property destruction caused by cigarettes (Choice D).

(Choice C) While the adult's violation of the statute was the actual ("but-for") cause of the property destruction, this violation was not a proximate (legal) cause of the property destruction since this type of harm was not a risk that made the adult's conduct tortious (Choice C).

Educational objective: Duty and breach are presumed under the doctrine of negligence per se when (1) the defendant violated a statute or ordinance, (2) the plaintiff suffered a type of harm that the statute or ordinance was intended to protect against, and (3) the plaintiff was in the class of persons intended to be protected by the statute or ordinance.

References

Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 14 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (negligence per se).
questions.zh-question:
一名成年人将一包香烟给了一名未成年人，该成年人误认为其是成年人。该未成年人将香烟带到附近的一处地产，爬上一堆栅栏柱，点燃一支香烟并开始吸食。此后不久，该未成年人无意中将点燃的香烟掉入了那堆栅栏柱中。该未成年人试图取回香烟将其熄灭，但未能成功。之后，该未成年人走开了。点燃的香烟随后引燃了栅栏柱，导致栅栏柱以及相邻的车库及其内部物品被毁。

该司法管辖区有一项严格责任法规，规定向未成年人提供香烟属轻罪。违反该法规可处以200美元罚款。

被毁财产的所有人对该成年人提起了过失诉讼。

以下哪项是该成年人对此诉讼最弱的抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 该成年人在给未成年人香烟时，并不知道其未成年。
zh-choices.B: 财产的毁损并非该法规旨在保护的损害类型。
zh-choices.C: 财产的毁损并非由成年人违反法规的行为所近因导致。
zh-choices.D: 财产所有人不属于该法规旨在保护的人群类别。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Negligence Per Se (过失本身)
核心原则：Negligence Per Se

在普通法中，如果被告违反了旨在保护特定人群免受特定伤害的法规，法院可以直接推定其存在义务 (Duty) 和 违约 (Breach)。

适用三要素：

  • 被告违反了法规 (Statutory Violation)。
  • 原告属于该法规旨在保护的人群 (Class of Persons)。
  • 伤害属于该法规旨在防止的类型 (Class of Risks/Harm)。
最弱的抗辩 (正确答案 A)

"我不知道他是未成年人"

为什么这是最弱的？
题目明确指出该法规是严格责任 (Strict Liability)。这意味着违规不需要意图 (Mens Rea) 或过失。只要你把烟给了未成年人，你就违反了法规。

既然违反法规是既定事实，且不需要证明被告的心理状态，那么“不知道对方年龄”在法律上是无效的抗辩。它无法否定“违反法规”这一事实，因此无法阻止 Negligence Per Se 的适用。

强有力的抗辩 (选项 B, C, D)

这三个选项之所以是“强”抗辩，是因为它们成功攻击了过失诉讼的必要元素：

  • 选项 B (伤害类型): 禁止未成年人吸烟的法律通常是为了保护健康，而不是防止火灾/财产损失。如果伤害类型不符，Negligence Per Se 不适用。
  • 选项 D (受保护人群): 法律旨在保护未成年人，而不是财产所有者。如果原告不在保护范围内，Negligence Per Se 不适用。
  • 选项 C (近因 Proximate Cause): 即使被告有过失，原告仍需证明该过失是损害的法律原因。被告可以辩称：给烟并不必然导致烧毁车库，这超出了可预见的风险范围。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
当题目问“最弱的抗辩 (Weakest Defense)”时，实际上是在问你：“以下哪个法律论点是完全站不住脚的？”

在本题中，面对 Strict Liability (严格责任) 法规，辩解“不知情”在法律上是毫无意义的，因此它是最弱的。而其他选项虽然未必一定能赢，但至少是法律上有效的切入点。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify weakest negligence per se defense

reason.en: Eliminates fault-based defenses such as lack of knowledge of the minor's age.
reason.zh: 排除以不知未成年年龄等为理由的过错抗辩。

reason.en: Establishes the predicate statutory breach for negligence per se.
reason.zh: 构成过失法定责任所要求的违法要件。

keywords.text: incorrectly believed to be an adult

reason.en: Sounds exculpatory but is irrelevant under a strict liability cigarette statute.
reason.zh: 看似可免责，但在严格责任法下并不成立。

A.text: did not know that the minor was underage

reason.zh: 因法规为严格责任，不知年龄不能成立抗辩。

label.zh: 损害不在法规保护范围

reason.zh: 主张财产火灾与供烟行为之间缺乏法律近因。

highlights.text: strict liability statute that makes it a misdemeanor to provide a minor with cigarettes

label.zh: 向未成年人供烟的严格责任法

reason.en: Makes the adult's lack of knowledge irrelevant and defeats choice A.
reason.zh: 使成年人不知年龄无效，从而否定A选项。

highlights.text: incorrectly believed to be an adult

reason.en: Mirrors choice A and tempts a fault-based defense that strict liability rejects.
reason.zh: 对应A选项，诱使考生采用严格责任下不成立的过错抗辩。

reason.zh: 支持B、C、D等更强抗辩，即法规旨在防止未成年人吸烟而非财产火灾。

highlights.text: WEAKEST defense to this action

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A shopping mall located near an interstate highway exit is surrounded by a paved parking area. Each entrance to the parking area has a sign reading, "City Ordinance: NO TRESPASSING from midnight to 6 a.m."
A weary cross-country traveler had begun to doze while driving. Concerned that he would cause a car accident, he looked for a place to sleep. At 2:00 a.m., the traveler saw the shopping mall from the road and exited the highway. In his exhausted state, the traveler failed to notice the city ordinance signs. The traveler pulled into the open gates of the parking area to rest and immediately fell asleep.
An hour later, the traveler suffered a serious personal injury when a light pole fell onto his car. Unbeknownst to the mall owner, a mall patron had backed her truck into the pole the previous day. The damage to the light pole was not readily visible upon a reasonable inspection. However, an inspection by the maintenance company hired by the mall owner would have revealed that the pole was dangerously off-balance.
The traveler sued the mall owner in a negligence action for damages stemming from personal injuries and property damage suffered when the light pole fell.
In a jurisdiction that follows the traditional approach regarding a land possessor's duty to land entrants, which of the following is likely to be the mall owner's best defense?

choices.A: The mall owner did not know of the risk posed by the light pole.
choices.B: The mall owner could not reasonably foresee that the traveler would enter the parking area.
choices.C: The traveler assumed the risk of injury when he entered the parking area at a prohibited time.
choices.D: The traveler's violation of the ordinance prohibiting trespassing was negligence per se.

questions.explanation:
Land possessor’s duty to land entrants
Invitees Inspect for unknown dangers, make safe or warn, & prevent harm from active operations
Licensees Warn of known latent defects & use reasonable care in active operations
Known or anticipated trespassers Warn of known artificial dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
Unknown or unanticipated trespassers No duty

To be liable for negligence, the defendant must have breached a duty owed to the plaintiff. Under the traditional approach, land possessors owe no duty to unknown or unanticipated trespassers.* But they do owe a limited duty to known or anticipated trespassers to:

• warn the trespasser about hidden, artificial dangers (ie, man-made dangers) that are known to the land possessor but unlikely to be discovered by the trespasser and

• use reasonable care while conducting activities on their land.

Here, the traveler trespassed when he entered the parking lot at 2:00 a.m. because entry is prohibited between midnight and 6:00 a.m. Not only was his presence foreseeable, it was anticipated—as evidenced by the “no trespassing” sign at each entrance—so the mall owner owed a limited duty of care (Choice A). But since the mall owner did not know of the risk posed by the light pole, the mall owner did not breach any duty owed to the traveler and so cannot be liable for negligence. Therefore, that is the mall owner’s best defense.

*The traditional approach is followed in about half the jurisdictions. The other half follow the modern approach, under which land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants (except flagrant trespassers).

(Choice C) Implied assumption of the risk arises when a plaintiff voluntarily encounters a known, specific risk. Here, the traveler did not know of the risk posed by the light pole. But even if he had, in most comparative fault jurisdictions (the default rule on the MBE), a plaintiff’s assumption of the risk merely reduces recovery.

(Choice D) The traveler’s violation of the ordinance was not negligence per se since he suffered as a result of the damaged light pole was likely not of the type that the “no trespassing” ordinance sought to prevent. Even if it were, this would only establish that he was contributorily negligent, which would reduce (but not bar) his recovery.

Educational objective:
A land possessor owes a duty to known or anticipated trespassers to (1) warn them about hidden, artificial dangers that are known to the land possessor but unlikely to be discovered by trespassers and (2) exercise reasonable care while conducting activities on the land.

📌 Educational Objective

A land possessor owes a duty to known or anticipated trespassers to (1) warn them about hidden, artificial dangers that are known to the land possessor but unlikely to be discovered by trespassers and (2) exercise reasonable care while conducting activities on the land.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 337 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (duty to known trespassers).
questions.zh-question:
主题：侵权法（Torts）— 过失（Negligence）

题目：
一家位于州际高速公路出口附近的购物中心，周围有一片铺设好的停车场。停车场的每个入口都设有标牌，写着：“城市条例：午夜至上午6点禁止擅入（NO TRESPASSING）。”
一名疲惫的长途旅行者开车时已经开始打瞌睡。担心自己会引发交通事故，他开始寻找可以睡觉的地方。凌晨2点，旅行者从公路上看到了这家购物中心，并驶离高速公路。由于极度疲惫，他没有注意到这些城市条例标牌。旅行者把车开进停车场敞开的闸门内休息，并立刻睡着了。
一小时后，一根路灯杆倒塌砸中了他的车，导致旅行者遭受了严重的人身伤害。旅行中心所有人并不知情，购物中心的一名顾客在前一天曾将自己的卡车倒车撞到了这根灯杆上。对灯杆损坏情况进行合理检查时，并不能轻易看出损坏；但是，购物中心业主雇用的维护公司进行检查后，会发现该灯杆已经危险地失去平衡。
旅行者以过失（negligence）为由起诉购物中心业主，要求赔偿因路灯杆倒塌而遭受的人身伤害和财产损失。
在一个关于土地占有人对进入土地者所负义务、并遵循传统规则（traditional approach）的法域中，下列哪一项最可能是购物中心业主最好的抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 购物中心业主并不知道该路灯杆所造成的风险。
zh-choices.B: 购物中心业主无法合理预见旅行者会进入停车场。
zh-choices.C: 旅行者在被禁止的时间进入停车场时，已自愿承担了受伤风险（assumed the risk of injury）。
zh-choices.D: 旅行者违反禁止擅入（trespassing）的条例构成当然过失（negligence per se）。

reason.en: Selects the trespasser-duty framework that governs the analysis.
reason.zh: 决定适用哪套针对侵入者的占有人义务规则。

keywords.text: land possessor's duty to land entrants

reason.en: The core negligence issue is whether any duty was owed and breached.
reason.zh: 核心问题是占有人是否负有义务并已违反。

keywords.text: NO TRESPASSING from midnight to 6 a.m.

reason.en: Shows entry was prohibited yet trespassers were anticipated, not unknown.
reason.zh: 表明进入虽被禁止，但侵入者属可预期而非未知。

reason.en: Places the traveler on the property during the barred trespass period.
reason.zh: 表明旅行者在禁止侵入的时段进入场地。

keywords.text: not readily visible upon a reasonable inspection

reason.en: Characterizes the danger as hidden rather than obvious to entrants.
reason.zh: 说明危险属隐蔽缺陷而非显而易见。

reason.en: Frames the dispute as duty, breach, causation, and damages.
reason.zh: 将争点框定为义务、违反、因果关系与损害。

A.text: did not know of the risk

reason.en: Without knowledge of the hidden artificial danger, no duty to warn was breached.
reason.zh: 占有人不知隐蔽人为危险时，无警示义务违反。

reason.en: Identifies the man-made hazard that allegedly caused injury.
reason.zh: 指明据称造成伤害的人为危险源。

reason.en: Mischaracterizes an anticipated trespasser as an unknown entrant.
reason.zh: 将可预期侵入者误当作未知进入者。

reason.en: Targets whether the traveler's presence was foreseeable to the owner.
reason.zh: 针对所有者是否可预见该旅行者进入。

reason.en: Invites a total bar though the specific pole risk was unknown and comparative fault usually only reduces recovery.
reason.zh: 诱使考生认为可完全阻却诉请，但具体灯柱风险未知且比较过错通常仅减损。

reason.en: Links trespass timing to a complete defense rather than limited duty analysis.
reason.zh: 将违规时间误连至完全抗辩而非有限义务分析。

reason.en: Treats ordinance violation as automatic negligence though the harm type is unrelated.
reason.zh: 将条例违反当作自动过失，但损害类型与条例目的无关。

reason.en: Suggests contributory negligence bars liability instead of merely reducing damages.
reason.zh: 暗示共同过失可完全排除责任而非仅减少赔偿。

highlights.text: traditional approach regarding a land possessor's duty to land entrants

label.zh: 适用的侵入者义务框架

reason.en: Determines which category of entrant triggers which duty and breach test.
reason.zh: 决定进入者分类及相应的义务与违反标准。

highlights.text: NO TRESPASSING from midnight to 6 a.m.

reason.en: Signals trespassers were anticipated, triggering limited duty rather than no duty.
reason.zh: 表明侵入者可预期，触发有限义务而非无义务。

highlights.text: At 2:00 a.m., the traveler saw the shopping mall from the road and exited the highway.

reason.en: Establishes the traveler entered as a trespasser during the barred period.
reason.zh: 确立旅行者在禁止时段以侵入者身份进入。

highlights.text: Unbeknownst to the mall owner, a mall patron had backed her truck into the pole the previous day.

reason.en: Shows the possessor did not know of the hidden artificial danger central to breach.
reason.zh: 表明占有人不知该隐蔽人为危险，关乎是否构成义务违反。

highlights.text: which of the following is likely to be the mall owner's best defense?

reason.en: Requires selecting the defense that most fully defeats liability on these facts.
reason.zh: 要求选出在这些事实下最能排除责任的抗辩。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pedestrian who was blind took her guide dog to the veterinarian for a checkup. While she was waiting, she decided to get a coffee at the coffee shop across the street from the veterinarian's office. Without the assistance of her guide dog, the pedestrian left the veterinarian's office. She was able to find the crosswalk because it was just outside the entrance to the office. Once there, she pressed the crosswalk button on the light post. When the audible pedestrian signal indicated that it was safe to cross the street, the pedestrian stepped out into the crosswalk. Another person walking in the crosswalk accidentally bumped into the pedestrian, causing the pedestrian to unknowingly veer out of the crosswalk and into oncoming traffic. At the same time, the plaintiff was driving his car toward the pedestrian. In order to avoid hitting the pedestrian, the plaintiff swerved into a lamppost. The plaintiff sustained injuries as a result of the accident.
The plaintiff has filed a negligence action against the pedestrian to recover damages for his injuries.
Which of the following standards will the court apply to the pedestrian's conduct?

choices.A: Whether the pedestrian acted in good faith when she crossed the street without her guide dog.
choices.B: Whether the pedestrian exercised the care of a reasonably careful blind person.
choices.C: Whether the pedestrian exercised the care of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances.
choices.D: Whether the pedestrian used her best efforts to safely cross the street without her guide dog.

questions.explanation:
Standards of care for negligence
AdultMust act in same manner as ordinary, reasonable adult in similar circumstances
• Standard adjusted for physical disabilities, superior skill & knowledge, involuntary intoxication
• Standard not adjusted for mental & emotional disabilities, voluntary intoxication
ProfessionalMust demonstrate same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
• National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
ChildMust act in same manner as reasonable child of same age, intelligence & experience
• Adult standard applied to children engaged in dangerous adult activity
• Children under five years old incapable of negligence

*A modern trend applies a national standard of care to all physicians.

The standard of care most often imposed in negligence cases is that of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances. A defendant's mental or emotional disabilities are not considered in determining whether conduct was negligent unless the defendant is a child. This means that the conduct of defendant with a mental disability will be measured by the standard of someone of ordinary intelligence and knowledge.

However, a defendant's particular physical characteristics (eg, blindness) are considered. This means that the conduct of a defendant with a physical disability will be measured by the standard of a reasonably careful person with the same disability. Therefore, the standard that the court will apply to the pedestrian's conduct is whether she exercised the care of a reasonably careful blind person (Choice C).

(Choices A & D) The standard of care for negligence is an objective one, measured by what a reasonably prudent person with the same physical characteristics would have done. Whether a particular defendant acted in good faith or used his/her best efforts is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

In negligence cases, the conduct of a defendant with a physical disability (eg, blindness) will be measured by the standard of a reasonably careful person with the same disability.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical and Emotional Harm § 11 (2010) (standard of care for persons with a disability).
questions.zh-question:
一位失明行人带她的导盲犬去看兽医做检查。在等待期间，她决定去兽医办公室对面的咖啡店买杯咖啡。在没有导盲犬协助的情况下，该行人离开了兽医办公室。她能找到人行横道，因为它就在办公室入口外。到达那里后，她按下了灯柱上的人行横道按钮。当人行横道声音信号提示可以安全过马路时，该行人踏入了人行横道。另一位在人行横道上行走的人不小心撞到了这位行人，导致该行人无意中偏离了人行横道，进入了迎面而来的车流中。与此同时，原告正驾车朝该行人驶来。为了避免撞到该行人，原告紧急转向撞上了一根灯柱。原告因这次事故而受伤。

原告已对该行人提起过失之诉 (negligence action)，要求赔偿其所受的伤害。

法院将采用以下哪项标准来评判该行人的行为？

zh-choices.A: 该行人在没有导盲犬的情况下过马路时，是否本着善意行事。
zh-choices.B: 该行人是否尽到了一个具有合理注意义务的失明人士的注意义务。
zh-choices.C: 在该等情形下，该行人是否尽到了一个具有合理谨慎义务的人的注意义务。
zh-choices.D: 该行人在没有导盲犬的情况下，是否已尽其最大努力安全过马路。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Negligence: Standard of Care

正确答案：选项 B 该行人是否尽到了一个具有合理注意义务的失明人士的注意义务。
(Whether the pedestrian exercised the care of a reasonably careful blind person.)
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (Legal Rule)

在过失侵权 (Negligence) 案件中，一般的注意义务标准是“理性人标准” (Reasonable Person Standard)，即一个具有普通谨慎义务的人在类似情况下会如何行事。

这是一个客观标准 (Objective Standard)，通常不考虑被告个人的精神缺陷或智力水平。

⚠️ 关键例外：身体残疾 (Physical Disabilities)
如果被告患有身体残疾（如失明、耳聋、截肢等），法院会调整标准。新的标准是：“具有相同身体残疾的理性人” (Reasonable person with the same physical disability)。

🔍 题目解析 (Analysis)

本案中，被告（行人）是失明的 (Blind)。

  • 法院不会要求她像视力正常的人那样行事（那是不可能的）。
  • 法院也不会因为她失明就完全免除她的责任。
  • 正确的衡量尺度：法院会问，“一个谨慎的、失明的人在过马路时会怎么做？”

因此，选项 B 准确描述了这一经过调整的客观标准。

❌ 错误选项辨析
选项 错误原因
A & D
善意 / 最大努力
(Good faith / Best efforts)		 错误。过失是客观标准，不是主观标准。即使一个人“尽了最大努力”或“心地善良”，如果其行为客观上不符合理性人标准，仍构成过失。
C
普通理性人
(Reasonably prudent person)		 不准确。虽然这是基础标准，但对于身体残疾者，必须加上“具有相同残疾”这一限定词。如果不加限定，通常暗示是视力正常的普通人标准，这对盲人被告是不公平且法律上错误的。
🎓 MBE 拿分技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理 Standard of Care（注意义务标准）的问题时，请务必区分身体残疾与精神残疾：

  • 身体残疾 (Physical)：标准会调整。参考系是“有同样残疾的理性人”。
  • 精神/智力残疾 (Mental)：标准不会调整。参考系依然是“具有普通智力的理性人”。（除非被告是儿童）。
MBE Torts Review | UWORLD Source Analysis

reason.en: Blindness triggers a disability-adjusted negligence standard rather than the default reasonable-person test.
reason.zh: 失明会触发按残疾调整的过失注意义务标准，而非默认的合理人标准。

reason.en: Shows the pedestrian ordinarily relies on assistance tied to her physical disability.
reason.zh: 表明行人通常依赖与其身体残疾相关的辅助手段。

keywords.text: Without the assistance of her guide dog

reason.en: Sets the factual circumstances under which her care must still be judged.
reason.zh: 界定评价其注意义务时所处的事实情境。

reason.en: Signals the court must select the applicable objective standard of care.
reason.zh: 表明法院须确定适用的客观注意义务标准。

reason.en: Directly asks which negligence benchmark governs the pedestrian's conduct.
reason.zh: 直接询问应以何种过失注意义务基准评价行人行为。

reason.en: Identifies the ordinary adult activity for which the care standard is measured.
reason.zh: 标明应以何种注意义务标准衡量的日常成人活动。

reason.en: Negligence uses an objective reasonable-person test, not subjective good faith.
reason.zh: 过失采用客观合理人标准，而非主观善意。

reason.en: Mentions missing assistance but does not state the correct legal benchmark.
reason.zh: 提及缺少辅助，但未给出正确的法律评价基准。

reason.en: Correctly measures conduct by what a reasonable person with the same physical disability would do.
reason.zh: 正确以具有相同身体残疾的合理人之行为作为衡量标准。

C.text: reasonably prudent person under the circumstances

reason.en: States the default negligence standard but ignores the physical-disability adjustment.
reason.zh: 表述的是默认过失标准，却忽略了身体残疾的调整规则。

reason.en: Sounds complete, but still omits the required same-disability modification.
reason.zh: 看似完整，但仍遗漏了须按相同残疾调整的要求。

reason.en: Personal effort level is irrelevant; negligence compares conduct to an objective standard.
reason.zh: 个人努力程度无关；过失须以客观标准比较行为。

reason.en: Focuses on outcome effort rather than the legal standard the court must apply.
reason.zh: 关注结果性努力，而非法院须适用的法律标准。

highlights.text: A pedestrian who was blind

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
While driving his pickup truck with a friend riding in the open bed, the driver swerved, throwing his friend to the pavement. The friend sustained severe injuries. The friend had often ridden in the open bed of the truck, and on some of those occasions the driver had swerved to frighten his friend. The friend sued the driver to recover both compensatory damages for his injuries and punitive damages.
Which cause of action would NOT permit the friend to recover punitive damages?

choices.A: Assault.
choices.B: Battery.
choices.C: Negligence.
choices.D: Recklessness.

questions.explanation:
Recoverable personal-injury damages

Intentional torts Reckless torts Negligence
Compensatory damages
Nominal damages
Punitive damages

Damages in tort law fall into three main categories:

  • Compensatory (ie, actual) damages – money awarded to compensate the plaintiff for his/her actual loss or harm
  • Nominal damages – a trivial sum of money (eg, $1) awarded to vindicate the plaintiff's rights when no actual loss or harm occurred
  • Punitive (ie, exemplary) damages – money awarded to punish the defendant for outrageous, malicious, or evil conduct and to deter the defendant and others from engaging in similar conduct in the future

Compensatory damages are available for any tort. But nominal and punitive damages are only available for torts involving intentional conduct (eg, assault, battery) or reckless conduct (eg, reckless driving) (Choices A, B & D).* A plaintiff cannot recover nominal damages for negligence since this claim requires proof of actual harm. Punitive damages are also not recoverable for negligence because these damages are designed to punish and deter outrageous, malicious, or evil conduct—not unreasonable conduct.

*Punitive damages are prohibited in Nebraska and extremely limited in Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, and Washington.

📌 Educational Objective

Punitive damages are imposed to punish and deter outrageous, malicious, or evil conduct. As a result, punitive damages may be awarded for torts involving intentional or reckless conduct. But these damages cannot be awarded for negligence, which involves mere unreasonable conduct.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 908 cmt. b (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (availability of punitive damages).
questions.zh-question:
一名司机驾驶其皮卡车，其朋友坐在敞开的车斗里。司机突然转向，导致其朋友被甩到路面上。该朋友身受重伤。该朋友曾多次乘坐该卡车的敞开车斗，其中有几次司机曾故意突然转向以吓唬他。该朋友起诉司机，要求赔偿其伤害的补偿性损害赔偿和惩罚性损害赔偿。

下列哪一项诉因不允许该朋友获得惩罚性损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 侵犯人身罪。
zh-choices.B: 伤害罪。
zh-choices.C: 过失。
zh-choices.D: 鲁莽。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法：惩罚性损害赔偿的适用范围

正确答案：C (Negligence) 本题考查的核心在于：普通的一般过失（Simple Negligence）不足以支持惩罚性损害赔偿的请求。
法律原理解析

1. 损害赔偿的分类

在美国侵权法中，损害赔偿主要分为两类：

  • 补偿性损害赔偿 (Compensatory Damages)：旨在弥补原告的实际损失，使其恢复到受损前的状态。适用于所有侵权行为（包括过失）。
  • 惩罚性损害赔偿 (Punitive / Exemplary Damages)：旨在惩罚被告的恶劣行为并震慑未来类似的犯错。

2. 惩罚性赔偿的门槛

惩罚性赔偿不是为了补偿受害者，而是为了惩罚被告。因此，其适用门槛非常高。通常仅适用于以下行为：

  • 故意行为 (Intentional Conduct)：如殴打、袭击。
  • 鲁莽行为 (Reckless / Willful and Wanton Conduct)：明知有高度危险却故意无视。
  • 恶意行为 (Malicious Conduct)。

关键点：仅仅是“不小心”或“不合理”的普通过失（Negligence），法律认为不应当受到额外的金钱惩罚。

选项深度对比
诉因 (Cause of Action) 过错程度 (Fault Level) 能否获惩罚性赔偿?
过失 (Negligence) 不合理 (Unreasonable) 不能 (No)
侵犯人身 (Assault) 故意 (Intentional) 能 (Yes)
伤害 (Battery) 故意 (Intentional) 能 (Yes)
鲁莽 (Recklessness) 故意无视风险 (Willful/Wanton) 能 (Yes)

为什么排除其他选项？

题目问的是“哪一项不允许”获得惩罚性赔偿。

  • 选项 A (Assault) 和 B (Battery)：属于故意侵权（Intentional Torts）。被告有故意吓唬或接触的意图，行为恶劣，允许判给惩罚性赔偿。
  • 选项 D (Recklessness)：鲁莽意味着被告主观上知道风险却漠不关心（conscious disregard of a high risk）。这种心态比普通疏忽更恶劣，因此允许惩罚性赔偿。
💡MBE 考试技巧

在处理涉及 Damages (损害赔偿) 的题目时，请记住以下公式：

Punitive Damages = Bad State of Mind

如果被告仅仅是“笨拙”、“健忘”或“不小心”（即 Negligence），原告只能拿回医药费和误工费（Compensatory）。只有当被告表现出“邪恶”、“恶意”或“极度鲁莽”时，法院才会动用惩罚性赔偿。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pregnant woman, whose due date for the delivery of her viable fetus was less than a month away, was walking in a parking lot and looking at her cell phone. She was hit by a car driven by a police officer, who had just received word of an emergency and carelessly failed to see the woman. Several days later, the woman gave birth to a child who suffered neurological damage as a result of the accident.
The woman, on behalf of her child, brought a negligence suit against the police officer for damages associated with the physical injuries suffered by the child. The woman and the police officer were found to be equally at fault for the accident.
The jurisdiction has adopted a modified comparative fault statute that bars a plaintiff from recovery against a defendant whose fault is less than or equal to that of the plaintiff.
In the child's suit against the police officer, will the child be likely to recover for her injuries?

choices.A: No, because the child was in utero at the time of the accident.
choices.B: No, because the firefighters' rule applies to police officers.
choices.C: Yes, because the child was viable at the time of the accident.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman was not at greater fault than the police officer.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Scope of defendant's duty of care
Cardozo view
(majority rule)		 Duty owed only to persons who might be foreseeably harmed as a result of defendant's negligence (ie, persons within zone of foreseeable harm)
Andrews view
(minority rule)		 Duty owed to everyone on earth if anyone might be foreseeably harmed as a result of defendant's negligence

To recover in a negligence action, the plaintiff must establish four elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. The majority rule is that the defendant owes a duty of care to the plaintiff only if the plaintiff is a member of the class of persons who might be foreseeably harmed as a result of the defendant's negligent conduct (sometimes called "foreseeable plaintiffs"). If a pregnant woman is a member of this class, then a duty is also owed to her unborn child—but only if the fetus was viable at the time the injury occurred.

Here, the police officer owed a duty of care to the pregnant woman because it was foreseeable that someone in the parking lot might be harmed by the police officer's negligent driving. As a result, the police officer also owed a duty to the woman's child, who was unborn (ie, in utero) but viable at the time of the accident ((Choice C)). And since the police officer breached that duty by carelessly failing to see the woman and caused the child's neurological damage, the child can recover from the police officer for her injuries.*

*The result would be the same under the minority rule (Andrews view) because the scope of duty under this rule is much broader—it extends to everyone if anyone might be foreseeably harmed.

(Choice B) Although the firefighters' rule applies to police officers (and other emergency professionals), it does not excuse their negligence. Instead, it bars emergency professionals from recovering damages for injuries attributable to the special dangers of their job.

(Choice D) The woman and the police officer were equally at fault for the accident. So had the woman been the plaintiff, she could not recover under this jurisdiction's modified comparative fault statute. But the plaintiff in this action is the child—not the woman. And since a negligent parent's fault is not imputed (ie, assigned) to a child plaintiff in a suit against a third party, the woman's relative fault is of no consequence here.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the majority rule, a duty of care is owed to any person who might be foreseeably harmed by the defendant's negligent conduct. Additionally, any duty to a pregnant woman is also a duty to her unborn, viable child.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 281, cmt. c (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that an actor can only be negligent toward the class of persons who might be foreseeably harmed by his/her conduct).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A candidate for state senate campaigned by going door-to-door throughout his community. One day, the candidate visited the home of his wife's childhood friend. The friend was having an in-ground swimming pool installed in her backyard. After digging a deep hole, the pool contractor had temporarily suspended work due to a heavy rainstorm and had left the site without installing safety fencing around the hole.
As the candidate and the friend were talking, they saw the friend's five-year-old child fall into the hole. The candidate ran outside, jumped into the hole, and pushed the child to safety. However, the candidate fell backward into the hole and lay submerged for several minutes in standing water left by the rainstorm. He was rushed to the hospital where he lingered in and out of consciousness for two months and then died. In a statement to the press, the pool contractor falsely asserted that the candidate and the friend were at fault because they were "carrying on an extramarital affair instead of supervising the child."
The personal representative of the candidate's estate has brought a survival action against the pool contractor and seeks to recover damages for the candidate's medical expenses, loss of income, and pain and suffering, as well as for harm to the candidate's reputation as a result of defamation.
For which of the following is the personal representative LEAST likely to recover?

choices.A: Loss of income.
choices.B: Medical expenses.
choices.C: Pain and suffering.
choices.D: Reputational harm.

questions.explanation:
Civil actions for tortious death

Type of
action		Proper plaintiffRecoverable damages*
SurvivalDecedent's personal representative
  • Damages suffered by decedent prior to death
  • Eg, medical expenses, pain & suffering
Wrongful
death		Decedent's spouse, next of kin, or personal representative
  • Damages suffered by spouse or next of kin as a result of decedent's death (no pain & suffering)
  • Eg, loss of income, loss of companionship

*If jurisdiction allows both actions, double recovery not permitted.

At common law, a tort action was extinguished upon the death of either the tortfeasor or the victim. But most states today have enacted survival statutes that enable the personal representative of a decedent's estate to pursue any claims the decedent would have had at the time of death. This includes claims for damages resulting from both personal injury and property damage, such as:

  • the decedent's medical expenses from the time of injury to the time of death (Choice B)
  • the decedent's loss of income during this time (Choice A) and
  • the pain and suffering the decedent experienced as a result of his/her injury (Choice C).

However, most states do not allow survival of tort actions involving intangible personal interests—eg, defamation, invasion of privacy. The reason is that these actions are considered too personal to survive the decedent's death. Therefore, the candidate's personal representative is least likely to recover for reputational harm resulting from defamation.

📌 Educational Objective

The personal representative of a decedent's estate can bring a survival action to pursue claims the decedent would have had at the time of death, including claims for damages resulting from personal injury or property damage. But most states do not allow survival of tort actions involving intangible personal interests (eg, defamation).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 926 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (survival actions in tort).
questions.zh-question:
一位州参议员候选人在其社区挨家挨户进行竞选活动。一天，该候选人拜访了他妻子儿时的朋友家。这位朋友正在其后院安装一个地下游泳池。在挖了一个深坑后，泳池承包商因暴雨暂停了工作，并且在未在坑周围安装安全护栏的情况下离开了现场。

正当候选人和朋友交谈时，他们看到朋友五岁的孩子掉进了坑里。候选人跑出去，跳进坑里，将孩子推向安全地带。然而，候选人向后摔倒在坑中，并在暴雨留下的积水中浸泡了几分钟。他被紧急送往医院，在两个月中断断续续地处于昏迷状态，之后死亡。在一份对媒体的声明中，泳池承包商谎称候选人和朋友有过错，因为他们“有婚外情而没有看管孩子”。

候选人遗产的个人代表对泳池承包商提起了存续诉讼(survival action)，要求赔偿候选人的医疗费用、收入损失、痛苦与折磨，以及因诽谤(defamation)造成的名誉损害。

遗产的个人代表最不可能就以下哪一项获得赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 收入损失。
zh-choices.B: 医疗费用。
zh-choices.C: 痛苦与折磨。
zh-choices.D: 名誉损害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Survival Actions & Defamation

正确答案：D (名誉损害)

在存续诉讼中，涉及诽谤等“无形人身权益”的索赔通常最不可能获得赔偿。

核心法律依据
存续法规 (Survival Statutes)

在普通法（Common Law）中，侵权诉讼会随着受害人或侵权人的死亡而消灭。但现代大多数州颁布了存续法规，允许死者的遗产代表（Personal Representative）继续追究死者在死亡前本可以提起的索赔。

无形人身权益的例外 (Intangible Personal Interests)

虽然存续法规允许大多数侵权索赔（如过失导致的身体伤害）继续存在，但许多司法管辖区仍然保留了一个例外：

涉及高度个人化的无形权益诉讼，通常不会在受害人死后存续。

典型例子：诽谤 (Defamation)、侵犯隐私 (Invasion of Privacy)、恶意起诉 (Malicious Prosecution)。

理由：名誉被认为是极具个人属性的，一旦人去世，恢复名誉的需求在法律上被认为不再那么迫切或不再适用。

为何其他选项可获赔偿？

选项 A、B、C 均属于因过失 (Negligence) 造成的有形损害，是存续诉讼的核心赔偿范围：

A. 收入损失 (Loss of Income)： 死者从受伤之日到死亡之日期间本应获得的工资，属于遗产的资产。
B. 医疗费用 (Medical Expenses)： 死者生前产生的债务，遗产有权追偿。
C. 痛苦与折磨 (Pain and Suffering)： 死者在受伤后、死亡前实际经历的痛苦。这是存续诉讼与非正常死亡诉讼（Wrongful Death）的关键区别之一。
考点辨析：存续 vs. 非正常死亡
比较项目 存续诉讼
(Survival Action)		 非正常死亡诉讼
(Wrongful Death)
关注点 死者生前遭受的损害 家属死后遭受的损失
常见赔偿 医疗费、生前误工费、生前的痛苦与折磨 丧葬费、家属失去的经济支持、失去的陪伴(Consortium)
诽谤索赔 通常不允许 (视为人身依附性过强) 不适用 (不能诽谤死人)
💡 MBE 解题技巧

当题目问“最不可能 (LEAST likely) 获得赔偿”时，通常是在考察一般规则的例外情况。

在涉及死亡的侵权题目中，请牢记：

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A woman who was driving down a busy street was lost, but she did not want to stop to figure out where she was going. Instead, she used her knees to control the steering wheel while she pulled up a map on her smartphone. As the woman approached an intersection, a truck driver coming from the opposite direction tried to make an illegal U-turn in front of her car. The woman looked up from her smartphone and immediately tried to grasp her steering wheel, but she was unable to swerve out of the way in time, so the truck crashed into her car.
The woman filed a negligence action against the truck driver to recover $100,000 in damages for injuries sustained in the accident. At trial, the trier of fact established that the woman and the truck driver were equally at fault.
Which of the following is an accurate statement of the damages that the woman can recover?

choices.A: In a contributory negligence jurisdiction, the woman can recover $50,000.
choices.B: In a modified comparative-negligence jurisdiction, the woman can recover $50,000.
choices.C: In a modified comparative-negligence jurisdiction, the woman can recover nothing.
choices.D: In a pure comparative-negligence jurisdiction, the woman can recover nothing.

*Default rule on MBE; π = plaintiff, Δ = defendant

In traditional contributory-negligence jurisdictions, a plaintiff who fails to use reasonable care for his/her own safety and thereby contributes to his/her own injury is barred from recovering damages. However, almost all jurisdictions have adopted some form of comparative fault (ie, comparative negligence). There are two forms of comparative fault:

  • Pure comparative fault (default rule on the MBE) – recovery is reduced by the plaintiff's percentage of fault
  • Modified comparative fault – the same as pure comparative fault, except that recovery is barred if the plaintiff's fault exceeds 50%

Here, the woman sought to recover $100,000 in damages from the truck driver. The trier of fact established that the woman and the truck driver were equally at fault for the accident.

  • In a contributory negligence jurisdiction, the woman's fault would preclude her from recovering any damages (Choice A).
  • In a pure comparative-fault jurisdiction, the woman's full damages would be calculated by the trier of fact and then reduced by the proportion that the plaintiff's fault bears to the total harm ($100,000 - $50,000 = $50,000) (Choice B).
  • In a modified comparative-fault jurisdiction the woman can recover because her fault did not exceed 50% (Choice C). * However, her total damages will be reduced by her percentage of fault ($100,000 - $50,000 = $50,000).

Therefore, the most accurate statement of damages is that the woman can recover $50,000 in a modified comparative-fault jurisdiction.

*This is the view in the vast majority of modified comparative-fault jurisdictions. However, in a small minority of these jurisdictions, a plaintiff recovers nothing when the plaintiff and defendant are equally at fault.

📌 Educational Objective

In a pure comparative-fault jurisdiction, recovery is reduced by the plaintiff's percentage of fault. The same is true for a modified comparative-fault jurisdiction, except that recovery is barred if the plaintiff's fault exceeds 50%.

📚 References
  • 57B Am. Jur. 2d Negligence § 954 (2020) (comparative negligence, generally).

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A patient who had suffered a severe fracture of her leg was treated by an orthopedist, who set the patient's leg and put it in a cast. When the leg continued to bother the patient six months later, she consulted a second orthopedist in the same town. The second orthopedist surgically inserted a pin to facilitate healing.
The patient brought a malpractice action against the first orthopedist, claiming that he should have surgically inserted a pin at the time of initial treatment.
The only evidence that the patient offered in support of her malpractice claim was the testimony of the second orthopedist, as follows:
In response to the question "Would you have inserted a pin initially?" the second orthopedist testified, "I personally would not have been satisfied that the leg would heal properly without a pin."
At the close of the patient's evidence, the first orthopedist moved for judgment as a matter of law. Should the motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because the patient has introduced evidence that the first orthopedist failed to give the care that the second orthopedist would have provided.
choices.B: No, because the second orthopedist practices in the same town and field of specialty as the first orthopedist.
choices.C: Yes, because the patient has failed to introduce evidence that the first orthopedist's care fell below the professional standard of care.
choices.D: Yes, because the second orthopedist also treated the patient and is thus not sufficiently objective to offer expert testimony.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Elements of professional malpractice
DutyAll professionals (eg, physicians, lawyers, nurses) owe clients professional standard of care
BreachProfessional failed to exercise same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
  • National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
CausationBreach actually & proximately caused plaintiff's harm
DamagesPlaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, personal injury or property damage)

*A modern trend applies a national standard of care to all physicians.

All professionals owe their clients a professional standard of care. For most professionals, this means that they must demonstrate the same knowledge, skill, and care as a normal member of the profession in a similar community. However, medical specialists (eg, orthopedists) are held to a national standard of care. Any professional whose conduct falls below the applicable standard of care and causes the plaintiff physical harm is liable for malpractice (a specialized negligence claim).

Here, the first orthopedist set the patient's fractured leg and put it in a cast without inserting a pin. In the patient's malpractice action, a second orthopedist testified that he personally would not have been satisfied that the leg would heal without a pin. However, this testimony does not establish that the first orthopedist failed to provide the same level of care as normal orthopedists nationwide ((Choice C)). And since the patient has offered no other evidence to support her claim, the court should grant the first orthopedist's motion for judgment as a matter of law.

(Choice B) The fact that both orthopedists practice in the same town and field shows that they are comparable professionals in similar communities—but a national standard of care applies here. And the second orthopedist's testimony as to his personal standard of care does not prove that the first orthopedist breached a national (or community) standard of care.

(Choice D) The fact that the second orthopedist also treated the patient does not bar his expert testimony establishing breach of the applicable standard of care. However, his testimony failed to do so.

📌 Educational Objective

Most professionals are required to demonstrate the same knowledge, skill and care as a normal member of the profession in a similar community. But medical specialists (eg, orthopedists) are held to a national standard.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 299A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining the professional standard of care in malpractice cases).
  • O'Neil v. Great Plains Women's Clinic, Inc., 759 F.2d 787, 789-91 (10th Cir. 1985) (applying a national standard of care in a malpractice action against a specialist).
questions.zh-question:
一名腿部严重骨折的患者由一位骨科医生治疗，该医生为患者的腿部进行了复位并打上了石膏。六个月后，当患者的腿部仍然感到不适时，她咨询了同一城镇的第二位骨科医生。第二位骨科医生通过外科手术植入了一枚钢钉以促进愈合。

患者对第一位骨科医生提起了医疗事故诉讼，声称他本应在初步治疗时就通过外科手术植入钢钉。

患者为支持其医疗事故索赔所提供的唯一证据是第二位骨科医生的证词，内容如下：

在回答“您当初会植入钢钉吗？”这个问题时，第二位骨科医生作证说：“就我个人而言，若不植入钢钉，我不会对腿部能正常愈合感到放心。”

在患者方证据出示完毕后，第一位骨科医生请求作出法律问题判决。该动议是否应被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为患者已提供证据，证明第一位骨科医生未能提供第二位骨科医生本会提供的治疗。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为第二位骨科医生与第一位骨科医生在同一城镇和同一专业领域执业。
zh-choices.C: 应该批准，因为患者未能提供证据证明第一位骨科医生的治疗低于专业注意标准。
zh-choices.D: 应该批准，因为第二位骨科医生也治疗了该患者，因此不够客观，无法提供专家证词。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Medical Malpractice
核心法律规则

专业过失 (Professional Negligence/Malpractice) 的证明责任：

原告必须证明：

  1. 义务 (Duty)： 医生对患者负有符合专业标准的注意义务。
  2. 违反 (Breach)： 医生的行为低于该专业标准。
  3. 因果关系 (Causation) 和 损害 (Damages)。

关键点： 证明“违反”通常需要专家证言 (Expert Testimony) 来确立客观的专业标准 (Standard of Care)，而不仅仅是专家的个人偏好。

案情深度解析

本题的核心在于“证据是否足以证明过失”。

原告（患者）起诉第一位骨科医生，理由是他没有在初次治疗时植入钢钉。为了赢得诉讼，原告必须出示证据证明：“按照骨科医生的专业标准，这种情况下必须（或应该）植入钢钉。”

然而，原告提供的唯一证据是第二位医生的证词：

"I personally would not have been satisfied that the leg would heal properly without a pin."
（“就我个人而言，若不植入钢钉，我不会对腿部能正常愈合感到放心。”）

为什么这个证据无效？

  • 这只是第二位医生的个人做法 (Personal Practice)，而不是行业标准 (Professional Standard)。
  • 医学上通常有多种治疗方案是可接受的。仅仅因为一位医生倾向于方案 A，并不意味着选择方案 B 的医生就是过失。
  • 由于原告未能确立“不打钢钉违反了医疗标准”，她未能完成举证责任，因此法院应直接判决被告胜诉 (Judgment as a Matter of Law)。
选项分析
选项 C (正确)

应批准动议。因为原告未能提供证据证明第一位医生的护理低于专业注意标准。第二位医生的证词仅反映了主观偏好，未确立客观的违反标准。

选项 A (错误)

法律并不要求医生提供“其他医生会提供的护理”，而是要求提供“符合行业最低标准”的护理。不同的医生可能有不同的治疗风格，只要都在标准范围内即可。

选项 B (错误)

虽然两位医生在同一城镇，但这与本题核心无关。对于专科医生（如骨科），现代趋势是适用全国标准 (National Standard)，而非地域标准。但即使适用地域标准，该选项也未解释为何原告证据不足。

选项 D (错误)

治疗过患者的医生完全可以作为专家证人。潜在的偏见 (Bias) 可能会影响陪审团对其证词权重的考量，但不会导致其证词在法律上无效或导致直接判决。

💡 MBE 答题技巧

在医疗事故题目中，仔细阅读专家证言的措辞：
  • 如果专家说：“大多数医生会...” 或 “标准做法是...” -> 这是有效的标准证据。
  • 如果专家说：“我个人会...” 或 “我习惯于...” -> 这通常不足以证明被告有过失。

记住：差异 (Difference) ≠ 过失 (Negligence)。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
Two coworkers agreed to carpool to work each day. The driver agreed to pick the passenger up each morning and return her home after work. In exchange, the passenger agreed to pay the driver a monthly fee. One morning, while on their way to work, the driver and the passenger drove down a city street. As they approached a busy intersection, the driver's cell phone made a beeping sound, indicating that she had received a text message. The driver glanced over at her cell phone, which was attached to her dashboard, to read the message. As a result, the driver failed to notice that she was driving through a red light. As the driver's vehicle entered the intersection, a car that had the right-of-way struck the vehicle on the passenger's side. The driver was not injured, but the passenger sustained a broken arm and bruised ribs. The passenger subsequently filed a negligence action against the driver.
What standard of care should the court apply to determine if the driver breached her duty to the passenger?

choices.A: Duty to refrain from gross or wanton and willful misconduct.
choices.B: Extraordinary care.
choices.C: Ordinary care.
choices.D: That of a reasonable person of similar age, intelligence, and experience.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Standards of care for negligence
Adult Must act in same manner as ordinary, reasonable adult in similar circumstances
  • Standard adjusted for physical disabilities, superior skill & knowledge, involuntary intoxication
  • Standard not adjusted for mental & emotional disabilities, voluntary intoxication
Professional Must demonstrate same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
  • National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
Child Must act in same manner as reasonable child of same age, intelligence & experience
  • Adult standard applied to children engaged in dangerous adult activity
  • Children under five years old incapable of negligence
*A modern trend applies a national standard of care to all physicians.

In negligence actions, the standard most often applied to determine if the defendant breached a duty to the plaintiff is one of ordinary care. Ordinary care is the care that a reasonably prudent person would use under the circumstances. In most jurisdictions, automobile drivers owe a duty of ordinary care to their passengers (those who pay money for the ride), as well as their guests (those who ride for free).

A few jurisdictions have enacted "guest statutes," under which an automobile driver's only duty to guests is to refrain from gross or wanton and willful misconduct. However, there is no indication that this jurisdiction has enacted such a statute. And even if it had, guest statutes do not apply to passengers (Choice A). Therefore, the court should apply the ordinary-care standard in this passenger's negligence action against the driver.

(Choice B) A duty of extraordinary care imposes liability on a defendant who is slightly negligent. This standard of care has been imposed on common carriers, innkeepers,* and bailees—but not automobile drivers.

*Most modern courts hold innkeepers (ie, hotel operators) to an ordinary standard of care.

(Choice D) The standard of care generally imposed upon a child, age five or older, is that of a reasonable child of similar age, intelligence, and experience. However, a child who engages in a high-risk activity usually undertaken by adults (eg, driving a car) is held to the same ordinary standard of care as an adult.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions, automobile drivers owe a duty of ordinary care to both their guests (who ride for free) and passengers (who pay money for the ride).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 7 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (duty).
questions.zh-question:
两名同事同意每天拼车上班。司机同意每天早上接乘客，下班后送她回家。作为交换，乘客同意向司机支付月费。一天早上，在上班途中，司机和乘客开车行驶在一条城市街道上。当她们接近一个繁忙的十字路口时，司机的手机发出了哔哔声，提示她收到了一条短信。司机瞥了一眼固定在仪表盘上的手机，去读短信。因此，司机未能注意到她正在闯红灯。当司机的车辆驶入十字路口时，一辆拥有路权的汽车撞到了车辆的乘客侧。司机没有受伤，但乘客手臂骨折，肋骨挫伤。乘客随后对司机提起了过失之诉。

法院应适用何种注意标准来确定司机是否违反了她对乘客的义务？

zh-choices.A: 避免重大过失或肆意和蓄意不当行为的义务。
zh-choices.B: 非凡的注意义务。
zh-choices.C: 普通的注意义务。
zh-choices.D: 与相似年龄、智力和经验的理性人相当的注意义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 侵权法考点解析

Negligence: Standard of Care
核心结论 (The Bottom Line) 在大多数司法管辖区，机动车驾驶员对所有乘客（无论是否付费）均负有普通的注意义务 (Ordinary Care)。

本题考察的是过失侵权（Negligence）中，驾驶员对车内乘客应承担何种程度的注意义务。

⚖️ 一般规则：理性人标准

在过失侵权案件中，默认的标准是“普通注意义务” (Ordinary Care)。即被告必须像一个在类似情况下的理性人 (Reasonably Prudent Person) 那样行事。

对于驾驶员而言，这意味着要遵守交通规则、保持专注、不看手机等。

⚠️ MBE 陷阱：客人法 (Guest Statutes)

这是本题最大的干扰项来源。少数司法管辖区存在《客人法》。

乘客类型 定义 注意标准 (若有客人法)
Guest (客人) 免费搭乘，出于社交好意 仅需避免重大过失 (Gross Negligence) 或肆意行为
Passenger (乘客) 付费或提供经济利益 普通注意义务 (Ordinary Care)

关键点：即使在有《客人法》的州，一旦乘客支付了费用（如本题中的 monthly fee），他们就不再是“客人”，而是“乘客”，司机必须承担更高的普通注意义务。

📝 本案分析

在本案中，乘客同意向司机支付月费 (monthly fee)。这一事实至关重要：

  1. 支付行为建立了商业或互利关系。
  2. 该乘客属于法律意义上的 Passenger 而非 Gratuitous Guest。
  3. 因此，无论该州是否有《客人法》，适用的标准都是普通注意义务 (Ordinary Care)。

司机看手机闯红灯的行为，显然违反了理性驾驶员应尽的普通注意义务。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A 重大过失 (Gross Negligence)
这是《客人法》下的标准。但本题中乘客付费了，不适用此低标准。
选项 B 非凡注意义务 (Extraordinary Care)
此标准通常仅适用于公共承运人 (Common Carriers)，如公交车、火车或某些情况下的旅馆经营者。私人拼车不属于公共承运。
选项 D 儿童/主观标准
虽然未成年人的注意标准通常参考同龄人，但当儿童从事成人活动 (Adult Activity)（如驾驶汽车）时，必须适用成年人的普通注意标准。况且题目暗示这是coworkers，通常为成年人。
✅ 正确答案：C 法院应适用普通的注意义务 (Ordinary Care)。
MBE 解题技巧：
看到 "Carpool" 和 "Payment" 时，立即排除 "Guest Statute" 的低标准。
驾驶汽车永远适用“理性成年人”标准，即使司机是新手或未成年。

A.text: gross or wanton and willful misconduct
